OP-001.defect_title: Divergent definitions of 'financial institution' across statute and AMLA note

operation.parameters: Designate the 31 U.S.C. 5312 enumerated definition as the canonical/base definition of 'financial institution' for the program-establishment regime, and record the AMLA 2020 sec. 6003 definition as a scoped variant that adopts 5312 by reference and adds two extensions (electronic fund transfer network; clearing and settlement system). Canonical anchor: 'financial institution' per 5312(a)(2) as extended by 5312(c). AMLA variant applies 'in this division' (Division F of Pub. L. 116-283) only.
operation.proposal: Establish one canonical definition node for 'financial institution' (31 U.S.C. 5312, subsection (a)(2) enumerated list plus the (c) additional inclusions) and attach the sec. 6003 AMLA definition as an explicitly scoped variant rather than a competing standalone definition. The variant is modeled as: (A) incorporates 5312 by reference, and (B) adds (i) an electronic fund transfer network and (ii) a clearing and settlement system, with scope limited to Division F of AMLA 2020.
operation.rationale: The divergence is not a genuine contradiction but a drawing artifact: 6003 does not replace 5312, it incorporates it by reference ('has the meaning given the term in section 5312') and then adds two items. Canonicalizing avoids two free-floating definitions of the same operative term while preserving both scopes. This is a fix-the-drawing move: no requirement changes, and the AMLA variant's narrower textual scope ('In this division') is preserved, not overridden.

citations.quote: (2) "financial institution" means-

"(5) Financial institution .-The term 'financial institution'- 

 "(A) has the meaning given the term in section 5312 of title 31, United States Code ; and 

 "(B) includes- 

 "(i) an electronic fund transfer network; and 

 "(ii) a clearing and settlement system.
In this division:

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The enacted-law hierarchy already requires the proposed semantic structure. 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) supplies the enumerated federal BSA definition of “financial institution,” while 5312(c) expressly adds institutions for purposes of the subchapter. AMLA 2020 §6003 does not displace that definition: its enacted text first incorporates the meaning in 31 U.S.C. 5312 and then adds electronic fund transfer networks and clearing and settlement systems. Its opening status-and-applicability control, “In this division,” confines that expanded variant to Division F. Placement of §6003 text in a statutory note or on the 31 U.S.C. 5311 source page does not broaden that express scope. Thus a base node for 5312, with a Division-F-only additive variant, represents the legal hierarchy and incorporation already prescribed by Congress rather than resolving an ambiguity through a new rule. The operation must not treat the two AMLA additions as globally amending 5312 or automatically subjecting those actors to every 5318(h) program rule. Nor does inclusion in the umbrella definition by itself override sector-specific applicability, exemptions, implementing regulations, agency delegations, or the FINRA SRO layer. For depository institutions, money services businesses, broker-dealers, and boundary-sector entities, those controls continue to determine the actual program duty. The operation changes only the drawing and preserves each source’s scope; it neither fills a missing duty nor changes operative requirements.

OP-003.defect_title: Divergent citation for GLBA 'Federal functional regulator' cross-reference (15 U.S.C. 6809 vs 12 U.S.C. 6809)

operation.parameters: Canonical statutory locator for the incorporated definition: 'section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (15 U.S.C. 6809)'. All blueprint cross-references to the defined term 'Federal functional regulator' should carry this single canonical U.S. Code locator; the '12 U.S.C. 6809' renderings in 31-usc-5318 (OBL-3 and the subsection (h) definition) are to be recorded as pin-cite variants of the same incorporated section 509 GLBA definition, not as a distinct authority.
operation.proposal: Register a single canonical definition record for 'Federal functional regulator' anchored to section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, with the U.S. Code locator normalized to '15 U.S.C. 6809'. Every obligation that incorporates the term (5311-OB-01 context, OBL-3, OBL-8/9/11/13, OBL-2) points to that one record. The divergent '12 U.S.C. 6809' pin-cite appearing inside 31-usc-5318 (OBL-3 and the subsection (h) definition) is mapped to the same canonical record as an editorial locator variance, so the blueprint no longer shows two competing statutory addresses for one incorporated definition.
operation.rationale: Both citations point to the SAME underlying incorporated authority: 'section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act'. The divergence is only in the parenthetical U.S. Code editorial locator (12 vs 15 U.S.C. 6809). Section 509 of GLBA is codified at 15 U.S.C. 6809, and the AMLA-2020 definition at 31-usc-5311 (the codifying, term-defining provision) uses '15 U.S.C. 6809'. This is a refactor-pass drawing fix: canonicalizing the locator is strictly meaning-preserving because the operative reference ('section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act') is identical in every instance and the term's meaning is fixed by that section regardless of the parenthetical. NOTE ON P3.5: selecting '15 U.S.C. 6809' as canonical is NOT a supersession call under newest-wins — the sources do not explicitly supersede one locator with the other. The choice rests on (a) the defining provision (31-usc-5311 (3)(A)) using 15 U.S.C. 6809 and (b) section 509 GLBA being codified at 15 U.S.C. 6809; the '12 U.S.C. 6809' rendering is treated as an apparent editorial mis-citation in the U.S. Code print, not an alternative live authority. To the extent the working group regards this as a resolution between two live source renderings, it is flagged as a policy/editorial choice, not a mechanical newest-wins outcome.

In prescribing the minimum standards under subparagraph (A), and in supervising and examining compliance with those standards, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the appropriate Federal functional regulator (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( 12 U.S.C. 6809 )) shall take into account the following:

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The current federal statutory baseline incorporates one definition: section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. Section 509 is codified at 15 U.S.C. 6809, and the defining provision reflected in 31 U.S.C. 5311 expressly uses that locator. The competing parenthetical in portions of 31 U.S.C. 5318 says “12 U.S.C. 6809,” but retains the same controlling section-509 reference. Under hierarchy and delegation, the enacted incorporation of section 509 controls the term’s meaning; the inconsistent U.S. Code parenthetical does not create a second definition or alter Treasury’s or a Federal functional regulator’s authority. Applicability is unchanged: the operation neither adds nor removes institutions, regulators, standards, supervisory functions, or examination duties. Status controls support use of current enacted law, but the source rendering itself contains the divergent locator and does not expressly supersede one rendering with the other. Thus the baseline strongly supports 15 U.S.C. 6809 as the accurate canonical locator while leaving an editorial ambiguity that the blueprint must disclose rather than silently treating as a newest-wins resolution. The operation is therefore a clarification, not a substantive change or fill-gap: it preserves the incorporated definition and maps the 12 U.S.C. rendering as a pin-cite variance. This remains a draft for human confirmation because selecting a single display locator is an editorial resolution not expressly commanded by the operative provisions.

OP-005.defect_title: Divergent 'account' definitions between bank CIP rule and broker-dealer CIP rule

operation.parameters: Extract the shared exclusion carve-outs common to both 'Account' definitions into a single normalized exclusion set referenced by both sector definitions: (i) accounts acquired through acquisition, merger, purchase of assets, or assumption of liabilities; and (ii) accounts opened to participate in an ERISA employee benefit plan.
operation.proposal: At blueprint level, factor the two verbatim-shared exclusions out of each sector 'Account' definition into one canonical exclusion block that both the bank and broker-dealer definitions incorporate by reference. This isolates the genuinely divergent operative core (covered relationship scope) from the identical exception scaffolding, so the drawing shows the shared and the divergent parts distinctly. The bank definition additionally excludes the check-cashing/wire/money-order 'no formal relationship' service case, which stays local to 31-cfr-1020.
operation.rationale: The defect is that the two definitions differ materially, but part of the apparent divergence is noise: the ERISA and acquisition/merger exclusions are word-for-word identical across sectors. Factoring these shared exceptions leaves the true, intended sectoral difference (deposit/credit/trust banking relationship vs. securities-transaction relationship) visible and un-obscured. This is a fix-the-drawing move: it does not change what either rule covers or excludes. It does NOT merge the definitions, because the covered-relationship cores are substantively different by design and merging would alter scope.

citations.quote:
Account does not include: 
 (i) A product or service where a formal banking relationship is not established with a person, such as check-cashing, wire transfer, or sale of a check or money order; 
 (ii) An account that the bank acquires through an acquisition, merger, purchase of assets, or assumption of liabilities; or 
 (iii) An account opened for the purpose of participating in an employee benefit plan established under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974.

Account does not include: 
 (i) An account that the broker-dealer acquires through any acquisition, merger, purchase of assets, or assumption of liabilities; or 
 (ii) An account opened for the purpose of participating in an employee benefit plan established under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation is limited to the derived blueprint and does not amend either operative definition. For the bank cell, the effective federal rule at 31 CFR 1020.100(a) already excludes accounts acquired through acquisition, merger, purchase of assets, or assumption of liabilities and accounts opened to participate in an ERISA employee benefit plan. For the broker-dealer cell, 31 CFR 1023.100(a) already requires the same two exclusion outcomes. The regulations are coequal, sector-specific FinCEN rules authorized within the federal BSA/CIP framework; neither delegates authority to the other, and the canonical block would not create a new cross-sector legal source. Applicability remains sector-specific: the bank definition retains its banking-relationship core and additional no-formal-relationship service exclusion, while the broker-dealer definition retains its securities-relationship core. Status controls support current-law treatment because the supplied provisions are operative regulations with verified quotations, not proposed rules. Factoring the common exclusions into a blueprint block referenced by both definitions therefore records outputs already required in each touched cell without expanding, narrowing, or merging their scopes. This is codification of duplicated operative content, provided the canonical block is expressly marked as a derived representational device rather than text that supersedes or independently authorizes either regulation.

OP-006.defect_title: Divergent 'account' definitions between bank CIP rule and broker-dealer CIP rule

operation.parameters: Record a typed 'sector-specialization-of-shared-CIP-element' relation linking the two 'Account' definitions as parallel scope-parameters of the single CIP pillar, each scoped only to its own § x220.
operation.proposal: Assert an explicit blueprint relation that the bank 'Account' and broker-dealer 'Account' definitions are sector-specific instantiations of the same abstract CIP program element ('the relationship that triggers customer identification'), differing intentionally in covered-relationship scope. Annotate that each definition is expressly limited to its own CIP section (§ 1020.220 / § 1023.220) by its own text, so the divergence is a deliberate scoping parameter, not an unreconciled conflict.
operation.rationale: The register frames the divergence as a defect, but the sources themselves scope each definition 'For purposes of § 1020.220' / 'For purposes of § 1023.220' — they are not competing definitions of one term but sector-local terms for structurally parallel pillars. RELATE-OBLIGATION makes that intended relationship legible without altering either. Newest-wins (P3.5) does not apply: there is no explicit supersession between the two parts, so any attempt to unify the covered-relationship core would be a policy choice, not a distillation — flagged accordingly and NOT proposed.

citations.quote: Account means a formal banking relationship established to provide or engage in services, dealings, or other financial transactions including a deposit account, a transaction or asset account, a credit account, or other extension of credit.

Account means a formal relationship with a broker-dealer established to effect transactions in securities, including, but not limited to, the purchase or sale of securities and securities loaned and borrowed activity, and to hold securities or other assets for safekeeping or as collateral.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The federal baseline supports, but does not itself expressly state, the proposed typed relation. At the hierarchy and delegation level, both provisions implement the federal CIP requirement through sector-specific regulations: 31 CFR 1020.220 requires a bank CIP, while 31 CFR 1023.220 requires a broker-dealer CIP. Applicability is expressly localized because each Part 1020 or Part 1023 definition of “Account” applies only for purposes of its corresponding § x220. Thus, the definitions govern different actors and covered relationships and do not supersede or conflict with one another. The baseline requires each sector to apply its own definition when determining which relationships trigger its CIP duties; it does not require either sector to adopt the other sector’s covered-relationship scope. The shared statutory and regulatory CIP structure supports modeling the definitions as parallel sector-specific scope parameters, but the supplied operative text does not expressly characterize them as instantiations of a single abstract element or affirm that every difference is intentional. Recording that ontology therefore clarifies the baseline rather than codifying an explicit legal relation. The operation must preserve both local definitions, exceptions, and applicability limits and must not unify their substantive scope. No new institution-level duty is made explicit, so fill_gap does not apply; no operative requirement is altered, so change does not apply. Final regulations, rather than enforcement evidence or proposed rules, provide the support, subject to human confirmation of status and the complete baseline as of the pinned 2026 date.

Both are drawn from the same FFIEC manual, so this is not a P3.5 source conflict requiring newest-wins; it is a single authority's fuller statement in the topical section versus a shorthand elsewhere. draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation touches only the federal depository-institution/FFIEC-manual layer. The two verified passages are from the same current examination manual: ffiec-man-cp-02 expressly defines internal controls as policies, procedures, and processes designed both to mitigate/manage ML/TF and other illicit-finance risks and to achieve BSA compliance, while ffiec-man-ra uses only the shorter parenthetical “policies, procedures, and processes.” Read in context, the topical internal-controls section supports applying the fuller formulation when the risk-assessment section refers to internal controls, and the shorter gloss does not affirmatively establish a conflicting scope. The baseline therefore supports the proposed unified reading, but it does not expressly require the drafting architecture of one canonical home plus a cross-reference; that architecture resolves ambiguity in the derived blueprint rather than codifying an explicit baseline command. This is not fill_gap because the operation adds no omitted actor duty and identifies no separate source establishing such a duty. Status controls matter: the FFIEC manual is official supervisory/examination material, not itself a substitute for governing statutes or regulations, so canonicalization cannot elevate its risk-mitigation wording into a new operative legal duty or extend it to MSBs, broker-dealers, or FINRA members. Subject to that ceiling, the operation is meaning-preserving clarification, not substantive change. Classification remains a draft for human confirmation because baseline_set_for has not been resolved and the underlying governing program rules were not supplied here.

operation.proposal: Define 'independent review' at blueprint level as the regulatory element the guidance actually describes, capturing the express carve-out that it is not a formal audit by a CPA or outside consultant. operation.rationale: The defect is a divergence in framing between the statutory phrase ('independent audit function to test programs') and the guidance's operative term ('independent review'). Pinning down the guidance term as a defined blueprint concept, with its express non-audit carve-out, removes ambiguity without altering what either source requires. This is meaning-preserving: the guidance itself supplies this definition.

operation.parameters: Canonical term 'agent' scoped per the 2016 guidance: includes authorized delegates, foreign agents or counterparties, and agents and sub-agents. Read together under their applicability conditions, the sources support treating foreign agents and counterparties as a proper subset of the broader 2016 guidance term rather than as a competing exhaustive definition. The baseline does not, however, expressly establish a cross-instrument canonical ontology or supersede the 2004 terminology, so the representational mapping is supported but not unambiguously required. Status controls also counsel retaining the 2004 foreign-agent category as live: no explicit rescission or newest-wins override is shown. This is therefore a clarification, provided the refactor preserves applicability and does not extend the 2004 foreign-specific due-diligence and monitoring duties to every domestic agent, authorized delegate, or sub-agent. OP-016.defect_title: 'compliance program' definition divergent across rules — CID/program contents included vs. not

operation.parameters: Canonical core: 'BSA compliance program' = a program each covered institution must develop and provide for the continued administration of, reasonably designed to assure/ensure and monitor compliance with the recordkeeping and reporting requirements of subchapter II of chapter 53 of title 31 U.S.C. (the Bank Secrecy Act) and Treasury's implementing regulations. The written/board-approved/minuted requirement, the four minimum contents (internal controls; independent testing; a designated day-to-day compliance coordinator; training), and the incorporated customer identification program are stated once as attributes of the canonical term and referenced by each agency instrument rather than re-articulated divergently.
operation.proposal: Introduce one canonical blueprint-level definition of 'BSA compliance program' whose invariant core is the program-establishment duty tied to the BSA recordkeeping/reporting subchapter and Treasury's implementing regulations, and to which the shared written/board-approved/minuted attribute, the four minimum contents, and the incorporated CIP attach. Each of the four agency extractions (OCC, Fed, FDIC, NCUA) points to this canonical entry instead of carrying its own divergent or absent articulation. OP-018.defect_title: 'Account' defined differently for bank CIP vs. broker-dealer CIP

operation.parameters: Do NOT collapse to a single shared definition. Instead register two sector-scoped canonical entries in the blueprint definition ledger: (1) Account[bank] scoped to §1020.220, and (2) Account[broker-dealer] scoped to §1023.220, each carrying its verbatim source text and its explicit scope tag. Add a ledger annotation recording that the term 'Account' is sector-relative and that the divergence is source-mandated, not a drawing artifact.
operation.proposal: Represent 'Account' as two explicitly scoped canonical definitions in the blueprint rather than one term with a hidden sector split. Each definition keeps its own verbatim text and a scope note ('for purposes of §1020.220' / 'for purposes of §1023.220'). The ledger flags them as intentionally distinct, so downstream obligations that reference 'Account' resolve to the correct sector-scoped meaning.
operation.rationale: The defect (D2) is a drawing problem: one label 'Account' silently carries two different meanings, inviting cross-sector conflation. This is a refactor-pass fix (fix the drawing, not the bricks): the two source definitions genuinely diverge in scope, and each is itself limited by its own text to a single Part ('For purposes of §1020.220' / 'For purposes of §1023.220'). Merging them would change what the law requires and is therefore prohibited. Canonicalizing as two scope-tagged entries preserves both meanings exactly while removing the ambiguity of a single shared label. The narrower substantive question of whether the sectors *should* share one definition is a policy choice outside this refactor pass and is not proposed here.

citations.quote: Account means a formal banking relationship established to provide or engage in services, dealings, or other financial transactions including a deposit account, a transaction or asset account, a credit account, or other extension of credit.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative federal regulations themselves establish two distinct, sector-limited meanings of “Account.” For banks, 31 CFR 1020.100(a), as used by §1020.220, defines the term by reference to a formal banking relationship and enumerated banking services. For broker-dealers, 31 CFR 1023.100(a), as used by §1023.220, defines it by reference to securities transactions and holding securities or assets. Under hierarchy and delegation, these codified regulations are controlling for their respective federal CIP regimes; neither definition may be generalized across sectors or displaced by a blueprint-level common meaning. Applicability is actor- and activity-specific: the bank definition governs bank CIP relationships, while the broker-dealer definition governs broker-dealer CIP relationships. The operation preserves the verbatim regulatory text, assigns each definition only to its operative sector, and records the resulting source-mandated divergence. It therefore reproduces an already-required distinction rather than adding, expanding, or harmonizing a duty. The law does not independently require Foundry to maintain a definition ledger, but the ledger operation has no substantive effect beyond accurately codifying the baseline meanings in the derived artifact. The divergence is real in the sources and reflects deliberately different actor scopes, so the fix is to make the differentiation explicit rather than harmonize the frequencies (which would change what the law requires). OP-020.defect_title: Divergent framing of what the detection/reporting policies must target across instruments

operation.parameters: Annotate O3's cross-reference 'transactions required under 31 U.S.C. 5318(g) and the implementing regulations thereunder' with its resolved referent: the suspicious transaction reporting (SAR) obligation. 31 U.S.C. 5318(g) is the statutory suspicious-activity-reporting authority; the transactions 'required' to be reported thereunder are suspicious transactions. Record the resolution so the blueprint carries the operative statutory citation AND its plain-language meaning as one node.
operation.proposal: Resolve the dangling statutory cross-reference in the operative rule text (Rule 3310(a)) so that the blueprint node for O3 shows that 'transactions required under 31 U.S.C. 5318(g) and the implementing regulations thereunder' resolves to the detection and reporting of suspicious transactions. This makes explicit that the rule-text cross-reference and the guidance's 'suspicious transactions' phrasing point to the same pillar, without altering either the operative citation or its scope.
operation.rationale: The divergence in D2 is a drawing defect, not a substantive one: the operative rule cross-references the statute (5318(g)) while the guidance restatements name the underlying subject (suspicious transactions). FINRA's own guidance treats these as identical — RN 17-40 states Rule 3310 requires broker-dealers 'to establish and implement policies and procedures that can be reasonably expected to detect and cause the reporting of suspicious transactions,' describing that as its incorporation of the same pillar the rule text frames via the statutory cross-reference. Resolving the cross-reference preserves the operative statutory anchor (higher specificity, load-bearing for enforcement) while surfacing its meaning, so the blueprint no longer presents two differently-specific framings of one pillar. This is meaning-preserving and does not change what the law requires.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: For the touched cell, the operative hierarchy is 31 U.S.C. 5318(g), its implementing broker-dealer SAR regulations, and FINRA Rule 3310(a). Rule 3310 expressly requires FINRA members to maintain policies and procedures reasonably expected to detect and cause reporting of transactions required under that statutory and regulatory chain. The statute supplies suspicious-transaction-reporting authority, while the implementing regulations determine which suspicious transactions are actually reportable. FINRA RN 17-40 and the FINRA AML FAQ interpretively restate the same Rule 3310 pillar as detecting and causing the reporting of “suspicious transactions.” Applicability is limited here to FINRA member broker-dealers subject to Rule 3310; the operation does not alter triggers, thresholds, exceptions, or the scope fixed by the implementing regulations. Status controls favor the rule text and incorporated statute/regulations as operative, with FINRA guidance serving only to corroborate the plain-language resolution. The baseline therefore supports the annotation, but the shorthand “suspicious transactions” is potentially broader than “transactions required” to be reported unless expressly tethered to 31 U.S.C. 5318(g) and its implementing regulations. Recording both formulations in one node, while preserving that tether, resolves an ambiguity of expression rather than adding or changing a duty. This is a draft human-classification aid because baseline_set_for is not implemented.

OP-022.defect_title: Divergent definitions of 'financial institution' across the codified BSA and AMLA 2020 definitional layers

operation.parameters: Designate 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) (as extended by 5312(c)(1)) as the base canonical definition of 'financial institution' for the blueprint. Record the AMLA 2020 §6003 formulation as a scoped extension node: '5312 meaning + (i) electronic fund transfer network + (ii) clearing and settlement system', tagged as applicable within Division F of Pub. L. 116-283 rather than as a subchapter-II-wide redefinition.
operation.proposal: Establish a single canonical 'financial institution' node anchored on the 5312 enumeration, and attach the §6003 additions (electronic fund transfer network; clearing and settlement system) as an explicitly-scoped extension layer keyed to the AMLA 2020 division. The blueprint stops presenting two free-floating divergent definitions of the same term and instead presents one base definition plus a labeled, source-scoped extension, so the narrower/broader relationship is visible rather than contradictory.
operation.rationale: The divergence is a drawing defect, not a substantive conflict: §6003 opens 'In this division' and defines the term for Division F of Pub. L. 116-283, while 5312 defines it 'In this subchapter'. They operate at different scopes, so canonicalizing on the 5312 base and recording §6003 as a scoped superset preserves exactly what each source requires without altering coverage. This is meaning-preserving: no institution is added to or removed from either source's reach. Note the scope boundary (division vs. subchapter) is drawn from the source headings, not asserted; if an Authority reads §6003 as reaching into subchapter II generally, that is a substantive reading beyond this refactor pass.

citations.quote: (2) "financial institution" means-
(c) Additional Definitions .-For purposes of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply:
In this division:

(5) Financial institution.--The term ``financial 
 institution''-- 
 (A) has the meaning given the term in section 5312 
 of title 31, United States Code; and 
 (B) includes-- 
 (i) an electronic fund transfer network; and 
 (ii) a clearing and settlement system.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The enacted statutory baseline already requires the proposed base-plus-scoped-extension relationship. In the legal hierarchy, 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2), supplemented by 5312(c)(1), supplies the operative definition of “financial institution” for subchapter II because 5312(c) expressly states “For purposes of this subchapter.” AMLA 2020 §6003 is an enacted Division F definition, introduced by “In this division,” and expressly incorporates the 5312 meaning before adding electronic fund transfer networks and clearing and settlement systems. Thus the additions apply through the Division F definitional layer; they do not, on the supplied authorities, amend the 5312 enumeration or create a subchapter-II-wide replacement definition. The applicability scopes are explicit rather than delegated to FinCEN, the banking agencies, the SEC, or FINRA, and no regulator or SRO source can enlarge those statutory scopes through this blueprint operation. Status controls support treating both provisions as current enacted law while preserving their distinct statutory locations and scopes. For depository institutions, money services businesses, and broker-dealers, the operation preserves existing 5312 coverage and merely records when the Division F superset applies. For electronic fund transfer networks and clearing and settlement systems, it records only the enacted Division F inclusion and does not assert general subchapter-II program coverage. The canonical node is therefore a meaning-preserving representation of what the baseline already commands, not a new coverage rule. A contrary claim that §6003 silently redefines “financial institution” throughout subchapter II would exceed the quoted applicability language and would require separate human legal resolution rather than being embedded in this refactor.

operation.proposal: Draw an explicit relation recording that the §6003 term is defined by reference to 5312 ('has the meaning given...') and then broadened by two additions. This makes the definitional dependency and the direction of broadening machine-traceable rather than leaving two nodes that merely repeat the same label.
operation.rationale: The §6003 text is itself a cross-referential definition that incorporates 5312 by reference and adds to it. Relating the nodes preserves that incorporation-plus-addition structure exactly and prevents a downstream reader from treating the two as independent competing definitions. Meaning-preserving; adds trace only.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The enacted statutory baseline expressly requires the proposed relation. AMLA 2020 §6003 defines “financial institution,” for Division F of Pub. L. 116-283, by first incorporating the meaning in 31 U.S.C. §5312 and then providing that the term “includes” an electronic fund transfer network and a clearing and settlement system. Normalize the '12 U.S.C. 6809' parenthetical appearing in 31-usc-5318 subsection (h)(2)(B) (OBL-3) and in amla-2020-uncodified OB-1 to the '15 U.S.C. 6809' target used everywhere else.
operation.proposal: Record at blueprint level that the cross-reference to 'section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act' resolves to a single codified target, 15 U.S.C. 6809, and flag the '12 U.S.C. 6809' parenthetical in the 5318(h)(2)(B) 'Factors' provision (OBL-3 / OB-1) as a scrivener's mis-citation of that same referenced provision. The blueprint's resolved-reference field for both the 5318(h) factors obligation and the AMLA 2020 uncodified mirror should point to 15 U.S.C. 6809, with a note preserving the verbatim '12 U.S.C. 6809' as-enacted text.
operation.rationale: The operative referent in every location is identical: 'section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act.' Only the parenthetical Code-title pointer differs (Title 12 vs Title 15). Section 509 of GLBA is in fact codified at 15 U.S.C. 6809, and the majority of extractions (31-usc-5311 (A), amla-2020 6003(3), 31-usc-5318 OBL-8/9/11) so cite it. The '12 U.S.C. 6809' instances point to a nonexistent/incorrect Title-12 location for the same section 509. Resolving the cross-reference to the correct codified target is meaning-preserving: the referenced substantive provision (GLBA sec. 509) does not change — only the blueprint's pointer is disambiguated. This fixes the drawing (a citation label), not the brick (what the law requires). NOTE ON P3.5: this is not a supersession conflict — both enacted texts refer to the same section 509; there is no newer-wins question. The '12 U.S.C. 6809' is a demonstrable mis-citation of an identifiable provision, not a competing live rule, so RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE (not a policy choice) is appropriate. The as-enacted '12 U.S.C. 6809' string is preserved as a note so the fix does not alter statutory text (ADR-003).

operation.proposal: Attach an explicit resolved cross-reference from the undefined term 'financial institution' in OBL-1 to its external definitional sources rather than leaving it '(undefined here)'. 31-usc-5318 sits in 'SUBCHAPTER II-RECORDS AND REPORTS ON MONETARY INSTRUMENTS TRANSACTIONS'; the operative program duty runs on 'financial institution', and the section text itself never defines it. This move draws the pointer to where the definition actually lives, so the material scope of the pillars mandate is traceable at blueprint level. Because the extraction records that the supplying definitions (5312, 6003) diverge, the resolved reference is annotated as multi-source with an unresolved-divergence flag rather than collapsed to a single canonical definition.
operation.rationale: The defect is that a core scope-bearing term in the operative statute has no local definition and is supplied only by cross-reference. RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE is the whitelist move for making an implicit/external definitional pointer explicit without changing what the law requires. This is a refactor-pass fix to the drawing: it makes the dependency legible. It does NOT pick which divergent definition wins — under P3.5, newest-wins would require explicit supersession in the sources, and none is shown here, so resolving the 5312/6003 divergence would be a policy choice and is deliberately left open (flagged, not decided).

OP-027.defect_title: 'reasonably designed risk-based programs' used as the pillars mandate but left undefined in statute

operation.parameters: Mark the term 'reasonably designed risk-based programs' in §5311(2) as a purpose-clause characterization whose operative content is located in the program-establishment rules elsewhere in subchapter II (the pillars provisions) rather than defined in §5311 itself; record the pointer as unresolved-within-excerpt.
operation.proposal: At blueprint level, annotate the undefined term 'reasonably designed risk-based programs' as a cross-reference to the substantive program-establishment obligations that supply its content, rather than treating §5311 as the definitional anchor. §5311 is a Declaration of purpose and by its own terms only states purposes; the pillars mandate's operative meaning lives in the program rules the purpose clause refers to. This resolves the defect as a mislocated-anchor problem: the term is not meant to be defined in §5311.
operation.rationale: The section header and lead-in confirm §5311 is purpose-only, so the absence of a definition here is expected drawing, not a substantive gap. The honest move is to point the reader from the purpose clause to wherever the program content is fixed — but the excerpted source does not itself contain the destination program-establishment provision, so the pointer must be logged as unresolved-within-excerpt for an Authority to complete. This fixes the drawing (relocating the definitional expectation off the purpose clause) without changing what the law requires.

citations.quote: It is the purpose of this subchapter (except section 5315) to-

(2) prevent the laundering of money and the financing of terrorism through the establishment by financial institutions of reasonably designed risk-based programs to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism;

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation does not add or alter a program-establishment duty. In the statutory hierarchy, 31 U.S.C. §5311 is expressly a declaration of the subchapter’s purposes: its lead-in says, “It is the purpose of this subchapter,” and §5311(2) describes prevention through establishment of reasonably designed risk-based programs. That status supports treating the phrase as a purpose-clause characterization rather than as a self-contained definition or operative pillars rule. The baseline therefore supports relocating the reader’s definitional expectation from §5311 to the operative statutory, regulatory, and applicable SRO program provisions. The support is nevertheless incomplete and ambiguous at the supplied-source level: the excerpt neither identifies nor verifies the destination provisions, their delegations, sector-specific applicability, or their current status as of the pinned 2026 date. Accordingly, the annotation may state that operative content must be obtained from applicable program-establishment rules elsewhere in the BSA framework, but it must retain “unresolved-within-excerpt” and must not assert a completed cross-reference until an Authority verifies the destinations. This is clarify rather than fill_gap because no new explicit duty is being derived from an already-established but unstated duty, and rather than change because the operation leaves all sector duties untouched. If the proposed annotation were read as claiming that §5311 itself creates the operative duty, or as identifying unverified destination rules, that claim would be unresolved and would route like change; the stated operation avoids that result by preserving the unresolved pointer.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The federal statutory baseline supports, but does not expressly require, the proposed relation. Section 5311(2) characterizes the subchapter’s purpose through financial institutions’ establishment of “reasonably designed risk-based programs,” while co-enacted Pub. L. 116-283, div. Applicability within the ratified scope follows through the statutory category of “financial institution,” encompassing the scoped depository institutions, money services businesses, and broker-dealers, subject to their respective implementing regimes. The operation is therefore meaning-preserving and improves navigability while retaining the undefined-term limitation. Because the baseline supports the connection but leaves its precise interpretive force ambiguous, the draft class is clarify rather than codify or fill_gap. This is a manual draft pending human confirmation and baseline-set resolution.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: Per spec/20 §3: the cell here is covered institutions' program-establishment duty to 'review and, as appropriate, incorporate' the AML/CFT priorities. Hierarchy/delegation: the term 'AML/CFT Priorities' is not a free-floating extraction artifact — it traces to a statutory mandate added by the AML Act of 2020 (§6101), codified within 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) (BSA program-mandate subchapter), directing FinCEN, in consultation with the federal banking agencies, SEC, and other stakeholders, to establish and publish government-wide AML/CFT priorities, which institutions' program rules already require reviewing/incorporating. Status controls: the duty to publish and periodically update priorities, and the correlative institutional review/incorporation duty, was already operative before this 2026 NPRM (FinCEN's 2021 AMLA-implementation priorities issuance and prior program-rule amendments); the NPRM's placeholder is an extraction/drafting gap, not a substantive void. Evidentiary ceiling: the operation's own citations are drawn from the NPRM preamble (a proposed rule) describing that it 'implements provisions of' the AML Act and that FinCEN acts 'as administrator of the BSA' — these establish context but do not themselves quote the statutory text creating 'AML/CFT Priorities.' A proposed rule cannot anchor a current-law claim (spec/20 §3 ceiling), so the precise statutory pin (31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(4), AML Act §6101) must be verified by the human classifier against the actual U.S. Code text before ratification, even though the underlying duty is not newly created by this move. Given the duty already exists at the statutory level and the operation only records where the referent lives (ADR-005 fill_gap), this is classified fill_gap rather than change/clarify/codify, but confidence is capped at medium pending citation verification.

But the excerpt does not itself equate the two phrases, does not enumerate a roster (e.g., which banking agencies; whether SEC/FINRA fall inside or outside 'the Agencies' for broker-dealer supervision, which matters given the ratified scope's inclusion of broker-dealers/FINRA), and does not state that 'the Agencies' is limited to entities receiving delegated authority versus being a broader coordination class. The operation's own rationale concedes this ('the precise enumerated roster is not spelled out ... any enumeration beyond "Federal banking regulators" would be a policy choice'). That concession is decisive: this is not a case where the source precisely and unambiguously fixes the referent (which would support fill_gap under ADR-005, citing the exact source establishing the duty/scope), nor one where the baseline is simply silent or points elsewhere (change), nor one where the indeterminacy is total and unresolvable from the text (unresolved). Rather, the baseline (the NPRM's own SUMMARY plus operative text) supports the general direction of the definition but leaves its precise boundary ambiguous — the textbook 'clarify' posture. No enforcement evidence is used to establish this duty (satisfying the evidentiary ceiling against enforcement-as-duty-source), and although the source is a proposed rule, the operation only describes/organizes the NPRM's own internal terminology rather than asserting a current-law obligation, so the 'proposed rules never anchor current-law claims' ceiling is not directly triggered — but this should be flagged since the underlying item is itself an NPRM and any downstream use of this definition as if it reflected settled current law would cross that ceiling.

Recording them as flatly '(undefined here)' misdescribes the regulation. RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE is the correct whitelist move because the defect is a reference that fails to reach its target definition. It is meaning-preserving: it changes nothing the law requires, only where the reader is directed to find the operative meaning. Because the definitional text is outside the excerpted spans, the operation identifies the link to be closed but cannot itself quote the definition — that is honestly noted as work for the Authority.

citations.quote: Terms applicable to a particular type of financial institution or specific part or subpart of this chapter are located in that part or subpart. Terms may have different meanings in different parts or subparts.

A covered financial institution shall take reasonable steps to ensure that any correspondent account established, maintained, administered, or managed by that covered financial institution in the United States for a foreign bank is not being used by that foreign bank to indirectly provide banking services to a foreign shell bank.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: Hierarchy & delegation: 31 CFR 1010.100 is the chapter-wide general-definitions provision and it expressly delegates: 'Terms applicable to a particular type of financial institution or specific part or subpart of this chapter are located in that part or subpart' (verified quote). This is itself a baseline rule of the CFR's own drafting convention — it already tells the reader that a term appearing undefined in Subpart A excerpts is not thereby void of meaning; the reader must look to the governing subpart. That interpretive duty (read subpart-specific terms in their own subpart) pre-exists the operation and is not created by it. Applicability: the substantive obligations in §§1010.610/.620/.630 (due-diligence program for correspondent accounts, due-diligence program for private banking accounts, shell-bank prohibition and screening) are unchanged in scope or content by this move — the operation only redirects where the reader finds the controlling definition, it does not alter who is covered or what must be done. Status controls: no amendment, repeal, or supersession is implicated; the operation is meaning-preserving per its own rationale. Evidentiary ceilings: the operation is well-grounded on the verified §1010.100 quote, but two weaknesses must be disclosed to the human classifier: (1) one supporting citation (from 31-cfr-1010-230-cdd) is marked verified:false and cannot itself establish the duty; (2) the specific target the operation names — 'subpart F, §1010.605' — is an assertion about chapter structure that is NOT contained in the excerpted corpus (§1010.605 text was never pulled in), so the Authority cannot yet confirm either the subpart label or that the six terms are in fact defined there rather than elsewhere in chapter X. Because the routing principle is baseline-established but the precise destination is unverified against the corpus, this is a fill_gap (the reader's duty to consult subpart-specific definitions already exists via §1010.100) rather than a codify — the operation itself cannot complete the link, it only records that one is owed and points at a candidate source pending Authority verification.

OP-052.defect_title: 'customer risk profile' used but undefined in Parts 1020 and 1023 CDD pillar

operation.parameters: Introduce a blueprint-level defined term 'customer risk profile' as a term-of-art anchored to the phrase used in the CDD pillar, scoped across Parts 1020 and 1023 (and, by parallel drafting, wherever the identical CDD pillar language recurs). The definition should be sourced from the surrounding regulatory text rather than authored: the customer risk profile is the risk understanding of a customer that the institution develops from understanding the nature and purpose of the customer relationship, and which the ongoing-monitoring and update duties then reference. The Authority must supply/ratify the operative definitional text; this move only flags that the term is used undefined and must be canonically defined once and referenced from both Parts.
operation.proposal: Flag 'customer risk profile' as an undefined term-of-art used in the CDD pillar of both Part 1020 (OB-1020.210-a-cdd-pillar and the parallel OB-1020.210-b program) and Part 1023 (OBL-7), and propose that the blueprint carry a single defined-term entry for it that both obligations reference, resolving the D4 defect that the term is used but nowhere defined.
operation.rationale: This is a refactor (fix-the-drawing) move: the sources use 'customer risk profile' identically in three places without defining it, so the defect is a definitional gap, not a substantive one. DEFINE-TERM makes explicit the meaning the sources already presuppose (a risk understanding developed from the nature/purpose of the relationship) without changing what the law requires. NOTE (ADR-003): the actual regulatory text does not itself define the term; the operative definition is a policy/drafting choice for the Authority. The blueprint should not invent a substantive definition that narrows or expands the CDD obligation — it should record the term as undefined-in-source and route the definitional content to the Authority. If the Authority declines to define it, the term stays undefined by source and the blueprint should mark it as such rather than fabricate content.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The current federal baseline in 31 CFR 1020.210(a) and (b) and 31 CFR 1023.210 requires covered banks and broker-dealers to maintain risk-based ongoing CDD procedures that include understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships for the purpose of developing a “customer risk profile.” The same surrounding provisions require ongoing monitoring and risk-based maintenance and updating of customer information. Thus, within each touched cell, operative regulations establish the underlying CDD duty and consistently use the term, while context supports reading it as the institution’s risk understanding developed from the nature and purpose of the relationship. However, the cited regulations do not supply a definition or require a single canonical defined-term entry. The operation therefore is not codification of an existing express definition and is not ADR-005 fill_gap, because no cited source establishes a duty to define the term. It is clarification insofar as the blueprint records an expressly nonbinding, source-traceable explanation of an ambiguously supported term and preserves the fact that it is undefined in source. The Authority must ratify any wording. If the entry instead fixes an exclusive, operative meaning, states that ongoing-monitoring provisions expressly reference the profile, or extends the definition to provisions not confirmed to contain identical language, that portion would be a change rather than clarification. Applicability is limited here to the Part 1020 bank and Part 1023 broker-dealer program cells; no separate FINRA duty is needed to support this definitional refactor.

operation.rationale: The term governs the fifth-pillar CDD duty yet is undefined in every operative instrument; only RN 17-40 supplies content. Note for the Authority: RN 17-40's phrasing is guidance, not operative rule text; adopting it as the canonical blueprint definition is a drawing-level choice, and if the working group judges that no source-supplied definition is sufficiently authoritative, this should route to classification rather than be treated as settled. The operation therefore resolves an ambiguity in an already applicable duty rather than codifying text already required verbatim, filling a missing duty, or creating a new duty. Applicability remains limited to FINRA members subject to Rule 3310 and capital acquisition brokers subject to CAB Rule 331. Human confirmation should verify the RN 17-40 span and assess whether later or higher-ranking FinCEN, SEC, or FINRA authority as of the pinned 2026 date supplies, displaces, or qualifies the formulation.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The current statutory baseline supports the canonical linkage, but its precise scope is not entirely explicit. AMLA-2020 §6003(3), an enacted statutory definition applicable within the AMLA division, defines “Federal functional regulator” by both (A) the meaning in GLBA §509, 15 U.S.C. 6809, and (B) an inclusion for any Federal regulator examining a financial institution for Bank Secrecy Act compliance. The 31 U.S.C. §5318 standards-setting provision, as amended through AMLA, expressly uses “appropriate Federal functional regulator” but its local parenthetical points only to GLBA §509. Thus hierarchy and delegation support using §6003(3), while the difference between the division-wide expanded definition and §5318’s narrower-looking parenthetical leaves ambiguity about whether clause (B) necessarily governs every codified §5318 use. The operation does not create or alter the underlying duties: the Secretary and appropriate regulator already must consider the listed factors when prescribing standards and supervising or examining compliance. It only creates a canonical blueprint node and resolves an implicit definitional link. Applicability is limited here to the ratified federal AML/CFT program scope for U.S. depository institutions, MSBs, and broker-dealers; it does not extend the operation to state regulators, FINRA as an SRO, or boundary sectors. Both supporting provisions are enacted law, and no status-control issue suggesting repeal, proposal-only status, or noncurrent authority is identified. Because the baseline supports but does not unambiguously compel importing §6003(3)(B) into every §5318 reference, the appropriate draft class is clarify rather than codify or fill_gap.

The verified parallel AMLA purpose statement establishes that policies, procedures, and controls shall be risk-based, but does not by itself establish the proposed detailed allocation formula. operation.parameters: Elevate a single canonical banking-agency 'minimum program content' general rule stating that each covered depository institution's BSA compliance program must, at a minimum, (1) provide for a system of internal controls to assure ongoing compliance; (2) provide for independent testing for compliance by institution personnel or an outside party; (3) designate an individual or individuals responsible for coordinating and monitoring day-to-day compliance; and (4) provide training for appropriate personnel. operation.proposal: At blueprint level, represent the four minimum program-content requirements (the 'four pillars') as ONE elevated general rule for depository-institution BSA programs, with the four banking-agency regulations linked to it as parallel instantiations per actor class (national banks/savings associations, state member banks, FDIC-supervised institutions, federally insured credit unions). The four verbatim pillar strings collapse to a single canonical minimum-content node; each agency obligation (OB/OBL-4 through -7) is re-expressed as 'applies the elevated pillar rule to [actor class]'. OP-060.defect_title: Correspondent-account/private-banking due diligence program duty duplicated across Part 1010 and sector Parts

operation.parameters: Bind the §1020.210(a)(1) and (b)(1) 'Complies with the requirements of §§ 1010.610 and 1010.620' cross-references to the now-canonical Part 1010 obligation nodes (post-merge OB-1010.610 / OB-1010.620) rather than restating or re-incorporating the operative program text.
operation.proposal: Resolve the bank program rule's incorporation of §§1010.610/1010.620 to a pointer at the single canonical Part 1010 duty node, so §1020.210 references the correspondent/private-banking program duty by cross-reference instead of appearing to restate it as a distinct program component.
operation.rationale: The description notes the sector program rules 'incorporate' the same duty as mandatory program components. §1020.210(a)(1)/(b)(1) already expresses this by cross-reference ('Complies with the requirements of §§ 1010.610 and 1010.620'), not by restatement — so the correct refactor is to wire that reference to the canonical node, not merge the bank rule away. This keeps the layered structure the law actually uses (Part 1010 states the duty; the sector rule adopts it) while removing any appearance that the duty lives in two operative homes. The §1020 quote is flagged unverified in the finding but is a verbatim span of the §1020.210(a)(1) source excerpt below.

A bank regulated by a Federal functional regulator shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) if it implements and maintains an anti-money laundering program that:

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: For each touched bank cell, the current federal regulatory baseline already uses the layered result produced by this operation: Part 1010 states the operative correspondent-account and private-banking due-diligence duties, while §1020.210(a)(1) and (b)(1) require the bank AML program to comply with §§1010.610 and 1010.620. Binding those sector-rule references to canonical Part 1010 obligation nodes therefore preserves, rather than adds to or alters, the legal hierarchy and delegation. Applicability remains actor-specific: §1020.210(a) addresses banks regulated by a Federal functional regulator, and §1020.210(b) addresses banks lacking one; the referenced Part 1010 duties apply when the relevant covered institution establishes, maintains, administers, or manages the specified correspondent or private-banking account. The operation does not remove the sector-level program condition, broaden covered actors, change triggers, or convert the referenced duties into independent §1020.210 duties. It merely represents the express incorporative cross-reference as a pointer to the single canonical duty nodes. The supplied materials treat the provisions as current regulations, not proposed rules. Although the exact §1020.210 cross-reference quotation is marked unverified in the finding, it is consistent with the extracted §1020.210 program actions and the verified current Part 1010 duties; human source verification remains appropriate before disposition. No fill-gap inference is needed because the incorporation is express.

OP-061.defect_title: Training requirement duplicated across program-pillar sources

operation.parameters: Designate OB-08 (in the compliance-program overview) as the canonical pillar-level statement of the training requirement; mark ffiec-man-cp-05-O1 as the section-level restatement of that same duty, linked to OB-08 by an 'elaborated-by / same-duty' relation. The training section (cp-05) is thereby positioned as the elaboration of the pillar established in cp-01, not an independent source of the duty.
operation.proposal: Relate the two identical training-requirement obligations so the blueprint records them as ONE duty stated in two places rather than two duties. OB-08 ('Training for appropriate personnel.' as one of the enumerated program requirements) is the pillar-level statement; ffiec-man-cp-05-O1 ('Banks must provide training for appropriate personnel.') is its restatement at the head of the dedicated training section. The relation flags cp-05-O1 as a restatement-of OB-08, and links the substantive elaboration obligations in cp-05 (O2-O10) as elaborations of that single pillar.
operation.rationale: The defect is duplication of the SAME mandatory training pillar across the overview and the dedicated section. Both quotes state the identical duty in the identical modality ('must'). A MERGE would collapse two distinct blueprint items and lose the fact that the source deliberately restates the pillar as the anchor for its detailed training guidance; the elaboration content in cp-05 (coverage, tailoring, board training, documentation) is genuinely additional and must not be deleted. RELATE-OBLIGATION is the correct move: it removes the appearance of two independent duties by recording that cp-05-O1 is a restatement of OB-08 and that cp-05 elaborates it, without altering, deleting, or reweighting any requirement. This is a drawing fix (how the blueprint represents the relationship), not a change to what the law requires.

citations.quote:
The BSA/AML compliance program must provide for the following requirements:[12]

A system of internal controls to assure ongoing compliance.
Training for appropriate personnel.
Banks must provide training for appropriate personnel.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: spec/20 §3 review: Hierarchy/delegation — the FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual's compliance-program overview (cp-01) enumerates the mandatory pillars derived from the underlying statutory/regulatory program-establishment requirements (e.g., 31 CFR 1020.210 and parallel federal banking-agency rules), and OB-08 ('Training for appropriate personnel.') is that pillar-level statement. The dedicated training section (cp-05) is structurally subordinate to, and elaborative of, that overview: its opening sentence (ffiec-man-cp-05-O1, 'Banks must provide training for appropriate personnel.') is verbatim-identical in actor, modality ('must'), and action to OB-08, and is immediately followed by ten sub-obligations (O2-O10) detailing scope, tailoring, board/officer training, documentation and periodicity — the classic overview-then-elaboration pattern the manual uses for every pillar. Applicability and status controls are identical across both cells (same actor 'Banks', same activity 'BSA/AML compliance program training pillar', no differing trigger, threshold, sunset, or jurisdictional split). Nothing in either provision suggests two independently created duties; the textual identity and the manual's own overview/detail architecture already establish that cp-05-O1 is a restatement of the same duty anchored at OB-08, not a second duty. The RELATE-OBLIGATION operation therefore does not alter what the law/guidance requires — it makes explicit, at the blueprint layer, a same-duty relationship the source itself already embodies. This tracks ADR-005 fill_gap: the operative training duty already exists and is established by ffiec-man-cp-01 OB-08 (itself derived from the statutory/regulatory BSA/AML program pillar requirement); the operation merely records that ffiec-man-cp-05-O1 is the section-head restatement of that pre-existing duty and that cp-05 O2-O10 are its elaboration, without deleting, merging, or reweighting anything.

OP-062.defect_title: Independent testing requirement duplicated across sources

operation.parameters: Designate OB-06 (program-overview pillar) as the canonical statement of the independent-testing pillar duty; mark cp03-o01 and the remaining cp03-o02..cp03-o09 obligations as the elaboration/detail layer that derives from OB-06. Relation type: OB-06 'is-elaborated-by' the ffiec-man-cp-03 obligation cluster; cp03-o01 'implements' OB-06.
operation.proposal: Record an explicit relation linking the pillar-level independent-testing obligation (OB-06) to the dedicated independent-testing section's lead obligation (cp03-o01) and its detail cluster. OB-06 remains the single normative pillar statement; the cp03 obligations are tagged as its operational elaboration rather than an independent restatement. This makes the apparent duplication a resolved cross-layer reference instead of two free-standing duties.
operation.rationale: The two locations are not truly redundant duties: OB-06 states the pillar requirement ('must provide for independent testing ... by bank personnel or by an outside party') while cp03-o01 (and o02-o09) supply who/how/frequency detail ('should be conducted by the internal audit department, outside auditors, consultants, or other qualified independent parties'). MERGE would flatten a genuine two-layer structure (pillar list vs. dedicated section) and lose the section's added specificity and softer 'should' modality; the honest fix is to relate them so the drawing shows one duty elaborated in two places, not two duties. No legal requirement changes.

citations.quote: Independent testing for compliance to be conducted by bank personnel or by an outside party.

The BSA/AML compliance program must provide for the following requirements:[12]

A system of internal controls to assure ongoing compliance.
Independent testing should be conducted by the internal audit department, outside auditors, consultants, or other qualified independent parties.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The federal BSA/AML program baseline applicable to U.S. depository institutions already requires a compliance program that provides for independent testing by bank personnel or an outside party. The FFIEC program overview restates that pillar using mandatory language, while the dedicated independent-testing section supplies supervisory elaboration concerning qualified and independent testers, conflicts, reporting, risk-based scope and frequency, and permissible staffing or collaborative arrangements. Applicability is therefore confined here to banks subject to the federal depository-institution program rules and the corresponding federal banking-agency/FFIEC supervisory layer; the operation does not reach MSBs, broker-dealers, or FINRA cells. Status controls matter: OB-06's mandatory summary reflects the operative program requirement, whereas cp03-o01 and much of cp03-o02..o09 use nonbinding 'should' or permissive 'may' language and cannot be elevated into additional mandatory pillars. The baseline supports treating the dedicated section as elaboration of the independent-testing pillar, but it does not prescribe canonical blueprint identifiers or an explicit 'is-elaborated-by'/'implements' relation, and the two extracted passages can otherwise appear to be separate duties. Recording that relation therefore clarifies the existing cross-layer structure without changing applicability, modality, or substance. Human review should ensure that 'implements' is not read to convert cp03 guidance or options into operative requirements and that OB-06 is canonical only within the derived blueprint, not a claim that the examination manual displaces the governing statutes and regulations.

OP-063.defect_title: Board-approval / responsibility for the program stated in multiple items

operation.parameters: Designate the board-approval / board-responsibility duty as a single general rule anchored in the program-structures item's Management and Oversight material (ffiec-man-ps-01), which states the board's primary responsibility explicitly, and treat the program-overview mention (ffiec-man-cp-01 OB-02) as a pointer to that general rule.
operation.proposal: Elevate the board-approval and board-primary-responsibility duty to a single general-rule statement located in the program-structures item, where the manual expressly assigns the board 'primary responsibility for ensuring that the bank has a comprehensive and effective BSA/AML compliance program and oversight framework.' The overview item's clause that the program 'must be written, approved by the board of directors, and noted in the board minutes' remains but is framed as a restatement/pointer to the elevated general rule rather than an independent obligation. This removes the duplicate free-standing statement of the same duty across two items while preserving every requirement (writing, board approval, board minutes, and board primary responsibility).
operation.rationale: The defect is duplication: the board-approval/board-responsibility duty appears both in the overview (ffiec-man-cp-01) and the structures (ffiec-man-ps-01) items. This is a drawing defect, not a substantive one. ELEVATE-GENERAL-RULE consolidates the scattered statements of one duty into a single authoritative locus without changing what the law requires. The structures item is the natural home because it contains the fullest articulation (board 'primary responsibility' and oversight framework); the overview clause is retained as a restatement so the writing/board-minutes specifics are not lost. No supersession or conflict is involved, so P3.5 is not triggered.

citations.quote: The BSA/AML compliance program[10] must be written, approved by the board of directors,[11] and noted in the board minutes.

The board of directors and senior management of a bank have different responsibilities and roles in overseeing, and managing BSA/AML compliance risk. The board of directors has primary responsibility for ensuring that the bank has a comprehensive and effective BSA/AML compliance program and oversight framework that is reasonably designed to
The board of directors is responsible for approving the BSA/AML compliance program and for overseeing the structure and management of the bank's BSA/AML compliance function.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation touches only the federal depository-institution program cell, not MSBs or broker-dealers. The verified FFIEC Manual text clearly states that a bank’s BSA/AML compliance program must be written, approved by its board, and noted in board minutes, and separately assigns the board responsibility for approval and oversight. Consolidating those statements into one locus while retaining the overview pointer does not alter applicability, modality, or the writing, approval, minutes, and oversight content. However, the supplied support consists of examination-manual material rather than the underlying statutes and regulations. Board approval appears as a mandatory requirement, while the broader formulation that the board has “primary responsibility” for a comprehensive and effective program may be a supervisory articulation whose precise operative status depends on the underlying agency regulations and delegations. Elevation is therefore supported but ambiguous unless the target preserves that source status and does not present the manual’s broader wording as an independently binding statutory or regulatory duty. This is not fill_gap because no previously implicit duty is being made explicit, and it is not change if the operation remains a status-preserving consolidation. Human review should confirm the applicable FinCEN and federal banking-agency program rules and ensure that the general rule distinguishes binding board approval from any broader supervisory expectation concerning primary responsibility and oversight.

OP-064.defect_title: Board-approval / responsibility for the program stated in multiple items

operation.parameters: Replace the duplicate free-standing statement in OB-02 with an explicit cross-reference to the elevated general rule in ffiec-man-ps-01 (board approval / board primary responsibility), retaining only the overview-specific 'written' and 'noted in the board minutes' components as locally-stated detail keyed to that general rule.
operation.proposal: Attach an explicit cross-reference from the overview item's board-approval clause (OB-02) to the elevated general rule in the program-structures item, so that the board-approval duty is stated once (in structures) and pointed to (from overview). The overview retains the written-and-board-minutes specifics but references the structures item for the substance of board approval and board primary responsibility, eliminating the implicit, unlabeled duplication.
operation.rationale: Composed with the ELEVATE-GENERAL-RULE move, this makes the relationship between the two items explicit rather than leaving two parallel statements a reader must reconcile. RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE converts the latent duplication into an intentional pointer, which is a pure drawing fix. It preserves all requirements and introduces no new duty.

citations.quote: The BSA/AML compliance program[10] must be written, approved by the board of directors,[11] and noted in the board minutes.
The board of directors is responsible for approving the BSA/AML compliance program and for overseeing the structure and management of the bank's BSA/AML compliance function.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation changes the blueprint’s presentation rather than the operative program duty. For U.S. banks, ffiec-man-cp-01 states that the BSA/AML compliance program must be written, board-approved, and noted in board minutes; ffiec-man-ps-01 separately states that the board is responsible for approval and oversight of the compliance function’s structure and management. The duplication leaves the relationship between the overview-specific details and the broader board-responsibility statement implicit, so making that relationship explicit is clarification rather than codification. Applicability remains limited to banks governed by the federal banking BSA/AML program framework; the operation does not extend the rule to MSBs, broker-dealers, or other sectors. Status controls must be preserved: the FFIEC manual statements are official supervisory/examination material and the cross-reference must not elevate them beyond the status of their underlying legal authorities. In particular, retaining the written and board-minutes details locally and referring to approval/oversight in structures must not convert supervisory phrasing into a new legal duty or broaden board responsibility. The result is also contingent on adoption of the associated ELEVATE-GENERAL-RULE operation; without that destination rule, the proposed pointer would be incomplete. Human review should confirm the underlying statutory/regulatory anchors and that the composed edits preserve modality and scope.

OP-065.defect_title: Designation of BSA compliance officer duplicated across sources

operation.parameters: Relation type: SAME-DUTY-ELABORATED-BY. OB-07 (the pillar-list statement of the compliance-officer designation requirement) is the general/overview statement; cp04-o1 (the board-designation obligation in the dedicated compliance-officer section) is the operative elaboration. Establish an explicit cross-link so the two are recognized as one duty at two levels of detail, not two independent duties.
operation.proposal: Record an explicit obligation relation binding the program-overview pillar item (OB-07: the BSA/AML compliance program 'must provide for ... [d]esignation of an individual or individuals responsible for coordinating and monitoring day-to-day compliance (BSA compliance officer)') to the dedicated compliance-officer section obligation (cp04-o1: 'The bank's board of directors must designate a qualified individual or individuals to serve as the BSA compliance officer'). The relation marks cp04-o1 as the detailed statement of the same designation duty that OB-07 lists as one of the program pillars, so a reader traverses from the pillar list to its full elaboration rather than treating them as separate mandates.
operation.rationale: The defect is a drawing problem, not a substance problem: the same designation duty is stated once in the pillar-list overview and once in the dedicated section, creating apparent duplication. A straight MERGE would be wrong because the two are not redundant restatements — OB-07 frames the duty as one of the program's required elements ('must provide for ... [d]esignation'), while cp04-o1 states who must act (the board 'must designate') and adds the qualification standard ('qualified'). Both are load-bearing and neither should be deleted. RELATE-OBLIGATION preserves both spans verbatim while making the overview→elaboration structure explicit, which resolves the perceived duplication without changing what the law requires. This is meaning-preserving and stays at blueprint level per ADR-003.

In the FFIEC manual, OB-07 states the program-element requirement generally, while cp04-o1 assigns the designation act to the bank’s board and adds that the designee must be qualified. Their shared subject, mandatory modality, and placement as overview and dedicated-section statements support treating them as one duty at different levels of detail. However, the supplied baseline does not itself contain the proposed explicit SAME-DUTY-ELABORATED-BY relation, and the actor phrasing and added qualification language leave some representational ambiguity about whether cp04-o1 is merely an elaboration or contains a distinct component. The cross-link therefore clarifies the baseline rather than adding, removing, or merging an operative obligation. Applicability is limited to banks/depository institutions governed by the referenced federal program framework; the operation does not establish an equivalent relation for MSBs, broker-dealers, or FINRA members. As a status control, the FFIEC examination manual is official supervisory material but does not independently supersede or expand controlling statutes and regulations. The operation is sound only as a meaning-preserving organization of duties anchored in the applicable underlying program rules; the supplied excerpts do not include the footnoted underlying authorities needed to confirm every agency-specific formulation.
