OP-066.defect_title: System of internal controls requirement duplicated across sources

operation.parameters: Relation type: elaboration/same-duty. OB-05 (pillar-list statement of the internal-controls requirement) is the canonical program-establishment obligation; ffiec-man-cp-02-O1 is the same duty restated with actor allocation (board via senior management) as the head of the dedicated internal-controls section.
operation.proposal: Record an explicit blueprint relation linking OB-05 and ffiec-man-cp-02-O1 as the SAME underlying duty ('provide for / maintain a system of internal controls to assure ongoing compliance with BSA regulatory requirements'), with OB-05 designated the canonical pillar statement and ffiec-man-cp-02-O1 designated the section-level elaboration that assigns responsibility to the board acting through senior management. The apparent duplication is thereby resolved as one obligation viewed from two structural positions (pillar enumeration vs. dedicated section) rather than two independent duties.
operation.rationale: The two locations are not conflicting or genuinely redundant substantive duties; they are the same requirement drawn in two places. Per the refactor-pass mandate to fix the drawing, not the bricks, RELATE-OBLIGATION makes the identity explicit without deleting either statement or changing what is required. A MERGE is inappropriate because the two statements do different structural work: OB-05 is the enumerated pillar in the program overview, while ffiec-man-cp-02-O1 carries the distinct actor-allocation content (board acting through senior management is ultimately responsible) that is not present in OB-05. Collapsing them would lose the responsibility-assignment nuance. The relation preserves both spans and their citations while eliminating the reader's inference that two separate obligations exist.

citations.quote:
The BSA/AML compliance program must provide for the following requirements:[12]

A system of internal controls to assure ongoing compliance.

The board of directors, acting through senior management, is ultimately responsible for ensuring that the bank maintains a system of internal controls to assure ongoing compliance with BSA regulatory requirements.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation touches only the federal depository-institution program/internal-controls cells represented by the two FFIEC manual passages; it does not extend to MSBs, broker-dealers, or FINRA members. OB-05 states the bank-level program requirement to provide for internal controls, while ffiec-man-cp-02-O1 restates substantially the same control objective and allocates ultimate responsibility to the board acting through senior management. Their shared subject, compliance objective, and bank applicability support treating the latter as a section-level elaboration rather than a second independent internal-controls pillar. The baseline materials supplied, however, do not expressly declare a SAME-duty relation, and the shift from a bank/program obligation ('provide for') to a governance responsibility ('ensure' the bank 'maintains') leaves some ambiguity as to whether O1 is solely an elaboration or also a distinct responsibility-allocation norm. Status controls also matter: both passages are from an official FFIEC examination manual, not the operative statute or agency program regulations. The proposed relation preserves that status and adds no duty, but a human should confirm the applicable agency regulations and delegations before treating the identity as compelled. Accordingly, the baseline supports the relation but does so implicitly and ambiguously, making clarify more appropriate than codify, fill_gap, or change.

Adding the structural cross-reference resolves the dangling relationship the manual leaves implicit and matches the manual's own referral pattern for the other program elements. draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The federal banking supervisory baseline already establishes the bank-level internal-controls pillar in ffiec-man-cp-01 OB-05 and treats ffiec-man-cp-02 as the dedicated treatment of that same subject. The repeated language—“system of internal controls to assure ongoing compliance”—and the section’s definition, board-responsibility statement, commensurateness guidance, and examiner factors support the proposed relationship. However, the supplied source does not expressly require an OB-05-to-section cross-reference or formally designate ffiec-man-cp-02 as an “authoritative expansion”; that structural relationship is implicit and therefore ambiguous. Adding the pointer clarifies the baseline rather than adding or removing an operative duty. Applicability remains limited to U.S. banks/depository institutions within the FFIEC federal banking supervisory layer; it does not extend the result to MSBs, broker-dealers, or FINRA. Status controls must be preserved: OB-05 and O1 use mandatory language, while O2–O7 largely state supervisory expectations or examiner activities using “should,” and the cross-reference must not elevate those statements into mandatory bank duties. Likewise, “authoritative elaboration” should mean canonical within the derived blueprint, not legal superiority over statutes or regulations. operation.rationale: This is a drawing-fix, not a bricks-fix: the same duty appears twice across two OCC bulletins, so a single blueprint node with dual provenance removes the D3 duplication without changing what the law requires. citations.quote: The agencies have independent authority to prescribe regulations requiring banks to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to assure and monitor their compliance with the requirements of the BSA.

The agencies have an independent mandate to prescribe regulations requiring banks to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to assure and monitor their compliance with the requirements of the BSA.

operation.composition_note: If the working group wants the merged node to use one canonical term for 'authority'/'mandate', that requires a separate SUBSTITUTE-TERM op — but only if the group first affirms the two words are meaning-preserving synonyms in context. I do not propose that substitution here because 'independent authority' and 'independent mandate' are not self-evidently identical in meaning (a mandate can connote a duty to act; authority connotes a power to act), and neither source defines either term. Flagging as a policy choice for the Authority rather than improvising a strictly meaning-preserving substitution I cannot verify.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The proposed MERGE cannot presently be shown to reproduce an output already required by the operative baseline. In hierarchy and delegation, the two OCC bulletins are official agency materials describing concurrent proposed rulemakings, not the statutes or effective regulations that confer or impose each agency’s rulemaking power or duty. Their verified quotations therefore do not by themselves establish a current operative obligation. Status controls are decisive: proposed rules may not anchor current-law claims. The underlying enabling statutes and effective agency-specific BSA program regulations as of the pinned 2026 date must be examined before determining whether OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and the Federal Reserve each has an operative authority, a mandate, or both. Applicability is also not identical: the 2024 source defines the agencies to include the Federal Reserve, while the 2026 source lists only OCC, FDIC, and NCUA. In addition, the extractions assign different modalities ('may' for authority versus 'must' for mandate), and the source nouns may distinguish power from duty. Consequently, a canonical node combining the full roster and the formulations 'authority/mandate' could silently synthesize a broader or different proposition rather than merely deduplicate one baseline duty. No enforcement evidence is offered, but the proposal ceiling alone prevents codify, clarify, or fill_gap on this record. The baseline is indeterminate until operative statutory delegation, applicability, and effective-status sources are resolved, so the draft routes as unresolved for human classification.

Both describe the identical drawing feature (CDD is added to the agencies' program rules to align with FinCEN's parallel rule), so a MERGE removes the duplicate representation without changing what the law requires. Note on newest-wins (P3.5): the two bulletins are not in conflict and neither explicitly supersedes the other — the 2026-11 language is a later, refined restatement of the 2024-19 statement of the same rulemaking, so selecting it to carry the merged node is an editorial/presentation choice for clarity, not a supersession determination.

For each touched federal banking-agency cell, the cited OCC bulletins describe a proposed rule—using “would add,” “proposed rule,” and “explicitly incorporates” in discussion of that proposal—not a final rule establishing current obligations. FinCEN’s existing parallel CDD regulations may independently impose applicable CDD duties, but they do not establish that those requirements have already been incorporated into each banking agency’s own program rule. Status controls therefore prevent the two proposal descriptions from anchoring a current-law canonical duty. The baseline supports a canonical node explicitly labeled as a proposed harmonization measure, but not the proposed current-duty formulation. No enforcement evidence is offered. Because the output as written would convert proposed text into a current operative requirement, the draft class is change rather than codify, clarify, or fill_gap.

The three instrument-level restatements (FIN-2016-G001, IR 2004-1, FIN-2006-G012) are recharacterized as pointers to that canonical node rather than as independent obligations, so the register carries one duty with three supporting citations instead of three parallel duties.

Treating that regulatory rule as the canonical node and the three guidance statements as downstream citations therefore codifies the hierarchy and removes drawing-level duplication. The operation must preserve regulatory applicability, exceptions, and distinct minimum program elements: in particular, the FAQ's independent-review requirement must remain a separately traceable component and must not be erased or converted into a broader independent-audit duty. Status controls also require treating 103.125 only as the former citation and confirming 1022.210 as operative on the pinned 2026 date. OP-072.defect_title: Independent review / testing pillar duplicated across instruments

operation.parameters: Designate the canonical statement of the MSB independent-review pillar obligation as the 31 CFR 1022.210 / 103.125(d)(4) program-element requirement: an MSB's AML program must provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate program, with scope and frequency commensurate with the risk of the financial services provided. operation.proposal: Collapse the two duplicate statements of the independent-review pillar into a single canonical obligation. Both OBL-06 and OBL-2 state the identical program-element duty ("Provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate program") grounded on 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1)(D) and 31 CFR 1022.210 / 103.125(d)(4). The merged obligation retains the verbatim core duty and absorbs the risk-based scope/frequency threshold that the FAQ quotes from the regulation, since that threshold is a regulatory qualifier on the same duty rather than a separate obligation.
operation.rationale: This is a drawing-level defect (D3): one duty appears twice across instruments on the same authority, so the blueprint double-counts a single legal requirement. MERGE is the whitelisted move for consolidating co-extensive obligations. It is meaning-preserving: the two texts are verbatim identical on the operative duty; the FAQ merely adds the regulation's own commensurate-with-risk qualifier, which does not change what the law requires. No newest-wins/supersession issue arises (P3.5) because there is no conflict — the sources agree. The FAQ's elaboration obligations (OBL-3, OBL-5 through OBL-11, review content/who/how-often) are NOT merged here; they are downstream detail on how the review is conducted, not restatements of the pillar duty, and should be RELATED to the canonical obligation in a separate move rather than folded in.

operation.rationale: The defect (D3) is verbatim duplication of the same duty across four instruments — a drawing defect, not a substantive one. This is meaning-preserving: the quoted spans are word-for-word identical for pillars (1), (3), and (4) across all four rules, and pillar (2) differs only in naming the institution's own personnel. No requirement is added, removed, or relaxed; the four agencies each continue to impose all four pillars. OP-080.defect_title: Rule 3310 program pillars duplicated across the rule text and multiple FINRA guidance restatements

operation.parameters: Canonical home for the FINRA Rule 3310 program-establishment pillars = the operative rule item FINRA-3310 (obligations O1-O8). All guidance restatements (RN 18-19, RN 17-40, RN 09-60, AML-FAQ, ORR) are demoted to non-authoritative pointers/references to the FINRA-3310 obligations rather than independent statements of the same duties.
operation.proposal: Designate FINRA-3310 (O1-O8) as the single canonical statement of the Rule 3310 program-establishment pillars (written program; senior-management approval; detect/report policies; internal-controls policies/procedures; independent testing; designation of AML compliance person; ongoing training; fifth-pillar ongoing CDD). Recast every duplicative program-pillar obligation extracted from the FINRA guidance items (RN 18-19, RN 17-40, RN 09-60, AML-FAQ, ORR) as restatements-of that canonical obligation set — i.e., the guidance items reference Rule 3310 rather than each independently asserting the duty. This collapses the one-duty-stated-across-many-instruments defect into one authoritative locus plus references.
operation.rationale: The guidance items themselves say they merely restate/incorporate Rule 3310, not create new duties: RN 17-40 states Rule 3310 'incorporat[es] the four pillars,' the ORR frames the list as 'FINRA Rule 3310 sets forth minimum standards ... requiring firms to,' and the FAQ says 'It requires firms to develop and implement a written AML compliance program.' Elevating the operative rule as the general/authoritative rule and pointing the restatements at it removes redundancy without changing what the law requires (refactor pass: fix the drawing). This does not touch the operative legal text (ADR-003); it is an advisory blueprint move about which item carries the duty of record.

OP-087.defect_title: MSB agent-allocation clause permits allocating responsibility yet imposes non-relievable sole responsibility

operation.parameters: Attach an explicit scope-relation between the permissive allocation duty (O14) and the non-relievable sole-responsibility duty (O15): O14 allocates responsibility for DEVELOPMENT of policies, procedures, and internal controls; O15 preserves each MSB's undischargeable responsibility for IMPLEMENTATION and for establishing/maintaining an effective program. The relation marks these as operating on different objects (development vs implementation/program-existence), not as a genuine conflict.
operation.proposal: Draw a RELATE-OBLIGATION edge recording that O14 and O15 are not contradictory but govern distinct objects. The regulation's own text scopes the allocation to 'responsibility for development of policies, procedures, and internal controls,' while the non-relievable clause is scoped to 'implementation of the requirements' and the obligation 'to establish and maintain an effective anti-money laundering program.' The blueprint should carry this development/implementation distinction so the apparent tension reads as a bounded permission sitting inside a retained duty, not as incompatible expectations.
operation.rationale: The defect is a drawing problem, not a substantive conflict: the two clauses share subjects (agent-only MSB and its principal) but not objects. 'Development' of the PPICs may be contractually allocated; 'implementation' and program existence remain each MSB's sole, non-relievable duty. Making that scope-split explicit at blueprint level resolves the perceived tension without changing what either clause requires. This is meaning-preserving and does not draft rule text (ADR-003).

In the immediately related status control, it separately provides that each MSB remains solely responsible for IMPLEMENTATION of the section's requirements and is not relieved of its obligation to establish and maintain an effective AML program. Thus, for both affected actors and activities, the controlling regulation already requires the proposed relation's output: allocation is bounded to development work and does not transfer or discharge each MSB's implementation and program-existence obligations. The operation records that legally operative scope split in the derived blueprint without changing modality, actor coverage, delegation, or substantive responsibility. FinCEN's existing-program-rule guidance confirms the non-relievable character of each MSB's responsibility but is not needed to create the duty. On the supplied record, no contrary higher-ranking authority, applicability limitation, or status issue makes the baseline indeterminate.

operation.proposal: At blueprint level, draw an explicit relation between the two obligations the extraction flagged as ambiguous: the permission to contractually allocate program responsibility (captured as an exception on fincen-ir-2004-1-ob-06 and reflected in OBL-02's own text about pointing to a contract) and the non-delegable, wholly-retained liability duty (OBL-02). The relation records that allocation and non-delegable liability are not in conflict: allocation redistributes who performs/develops policies, procedures and controls, while ultimate liability for having an effective program remains with each MSB and cannot be shed by contract.
operation.rationale: The sources themselves state both propositions in the same passage without contradiction: principals and agents 'may contractually allocate responsibility for developing policies, procedures and internal controls,' yet 'both the principal and its agents remain liable' and 'each MSB remains independently and wholly responsible.' The cited allocation provision permits specified program functions to be performed through domestic-agent arrangements, but it does not alter the regulated actor or extinguish that actor's program duty. Thus OBL-02 is a surviving constraint on any permitted allocation. Applicability is limited to entities qualifying as MSBs and, for the allocation permission, the relevant principal/domestic-agent relationship; it does not extend the proposition to foreign counterparties or non-MSB sectors. The 2004 release uses former 31 CFR 103.125 numbering, while the current guidance identifies 31 CFR 1022.210, so disposition should confirm the recodification and the precise scope of the exception attached to ob-06. That status issue does not appear to change the retained-responsibility rule because current guidance repeats it. The operation adds no duty, exception, or transfer of liability; it records a relationship already expressed by the baseline. The identified ambiguity is therefore representational in the extraction, not an ambiguity in the governing propositions.

OP-093.defect_title: MSB agent-allocation permission coexists with non-relievable sole-responsibility duty

operation.parameters: Relation type: scope-limitation / non-conflict. O14 (agent-principal may allocate development responsibility) is scoped to 'development of policies, procedures, and internal controls'; O15 (sole responsibility for implementation + non-relievable duty to maintain an effective program) governs a distinct subject matter (implementation and overall program-maintenance obligation). Annotate the blueprint edge so the allocation permission is expressly bounded to 'development' and does not reach 'implementation' or the non-relievable program-maintenance duty.
operation.proposal: Add an explicit RELATE-OBLIGATION edge between O14 and O15 recording that the two are non-conflicting because they address different subject matter: O14 permits allocation of DEVELOPMENT responsibility only, while O15 imposes non-allocable SOLE responsibility for IMPLEMENTATION and a non-relievable duty to maintain an effective program. The apparent tension noted in D1 is resolved at drawing-level by marking O14's scope as 'development' and O15's scope as 'implementation + overall program maintenance', so the allocation never touches the non-relievable duty.
operation.rationale: The source text itself draws the line: the allocation clause is expressly limited to 'responsibility for development of policies, procedures, and internal controls', and the very next sentence carves out 'implementation' and the 'obligation to establish and maintain an effective anti-money laundering program' as non-relievable. The defect is a drawing-level ambiguity (two obligations appearing to conflict) rather than a substantive conflict in the law. RELATE-OBLIGATION makes the source's own scoping explicit without changing what is required. This is meaning-preserving: no duty is added, removed, or softened. Note: this is not a P3.5 newest-wins situation — both duties are in the same provision and the reconciliation is drawn from the text's own subject-matter split, not a supersession policy choice.

Its allocation permission is textually limited to responsibility for “development of policies, procedures, and internal controls.” The immediately following language provides that each MSB remains solely responsible for implementation and that nothing in the allocation provision relieves any MSB of its obligation to establish and maintain an effective AML program. Thus, hierarchy and delegation are satisfied by a current, directly applicable FinCEN regulation; no lower-level source is needed to create the distinction. Applicability is limited to the agent-only MSB/principal arrangement addressed by the provision. The source’s status and supplied quotations are verified, with no indication that the rule is proposed, superseded, or otherwise inoperative. The baseline therefore already requires the proposed scope limitation: development responsibility may be allocated, but implementation responsibility and the effective-program obligation may not be relieved. Adding the RELATE-OBLIGATION edge codifies that required subject-matter boundary in the blueprint without adding, removing, or weakening a duty. OP-094.defect_title: Conflicting characterization of independent-testing personnel exception between RN 09-60 and Rule 3310 supplementary material

operation.parameters: Attach the independent-testing personnel-conflict prohibition (Rule 3310 Supplementary Material .01(c)) as a constraining sub-obligation of the O5 independent-testing obligation, so that the frequency requirement (O5) and the who-may-test prohibition are assembled into one linked obligation cluster rather than living in separate, unconnected blueprint nodes.
operation.proposal: Establish an explicit blueprint relation binding the personnel-conflict prohibition on independent testing to the independent-testing obligation O5. O5 currently captures the frequency dimension ('annual ... independent testing ... conducted by member personnel or by a qualified outside party') but the blueprint extraction for FINRA-3310 truncates before the Supplementary Material .01(c) prohibition. This RELATE-OBLIGATION makes the prohibition a first-class linked constraint on O5, so any restatement of the testing duty carries the who-may-test limb alongside the frequency limb.
operation.rationale: The defect is an assembled-duty tension: the frequency-only restatements omit the personnel-conflict prohibition, which currently exists only in Rule 3310 Supplementary Material .01(c) and RN 09-60. Relating the prohibition to O5 as a constraint fixes the drawing (how the obligation is assembled/linked) without changing what the law requires. The two sources are consistent in direction, so no P3.5 conflict resolution is involved. This is a pure structural link, not a new duty.

citations.quote:

(1) a person who performs the functions being tested,
(2) the designated anti-money laundering compliance person, or

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: For the touched cell, the operative baseline already requires the proposed linked output. FINRA Rule 3310 requires a member to provide for independent AML compliance testing, annually or, for the stated limited category of members, every two years. Supplementary Material .01(c), part of the same operative FINRA rule, expressly constrains that testing by prohibiting its performance by the tested-function personnel, the designated AML compliance person, or anyone reporting to either category. Thus the frequency limb and personnel-conflict limb apply to the same member testing activity; the latter qualifies who may satisfy the former. In hierarchy and delegation terms, the controlling anchor is the operative FINRA SRO rule and its supplementary material, not the regulatory notice. Applicability is limited to FINRA members subject to Rule 3310 and attaches whenever they perform the required independent testing, including under the biennial-frequency exception. Status controls support current-law treatment because the cited prohibition is in the operative rule rather than a proposal. RN 09-60 consistently corroborates the relationship but is unnecessary to establish it. The operation changes only the blueprint assembly by making an already-required constraint a linked sub-obligation of O5; it does not add, broaden, or resolve ambiguity in the underlying duty. Accordingly, the draft class is codify, subject to human confirmation because baseline_set_for resolution remains manual.

OP-096.defect_title: Regulation H uses 'state member banks' vs 'member bank/bank' without reconciling actor scope

operation.parameters: Canonical term: "member bank", defined per §208.2(g) as "a state bank that is a member of the Federal Reserve System" (with "state member bank" treated as a synonym of the same defined term).
operation.proposal: Canonicalize the covered-actor term for the BSA-program instrument to the single defined term supplied by §208.2(g), which expressly makes "State member bank" and "member bank" co-extensive. The blueprint records that §208.63(a)'s "all state member banks", §208.63(b)-(c)'s "member bank"/"Each bank", and §208.62's "bank" all denote this one defined class, and pins the definition to §208.2(g).
operation.rationale: The definitional conflict is only apparent: §208.2(g) states "State member bank or member bank means a state bank that is a member of the Federal Reserve System," so the two phrasings the defect flags are already stipulated to have identical extension within Part 208. Canonicalizing to the defined term reconciles the actor scope without changing what the law requires (P3 refactor constraint). This is meaning-preserving because it relies on the instrument's own definition rather than a policy choice.

citations.quote: (g) State member bank or member bank means a state bank that is a member of the Federal Reserve System.

The requirements of this part 208 govern State member banks and state banks applying for admission to membership in the Federal Reserve System (System) under section 9 of the Federal Reserve Act (Act)

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: Draft for human confirmation: the operative federal baseline already requires the proposed actor-scope equivalence. Within 12 CFR part 208, §208.2(g) expressly defines “State member bank or member bank” as “a state bank that is a member of the Federal Reserve System.” That controlling, instrument-internal definition applies to the terminology used in §§208.62–208.63. Accordingly, §208.63(a)’s “all state member banks,” §208.63(b)–(c)’s “member bank” and “Each bank,” and §208.62’s “bank” refer to the same defined class in this BSA-program context. Applicability is therefore limited to state banks that are members of the Federal Reserve System; the operation does not extend the duties to nonmember state banks, national banks, or other institution types. The source is an operative regulation issued by the Federal Reserve Board, not subordinate guidance, enforcement evidence, or a proposed rule. No delegation, hierarchy, or status conflict identified in the supplied materials displaces the express definition. Canonicalizing the blueprint to “member bank,” while retaining “state member bank” as its regulatory synonym and pinning both to §208.2(g), reproduces a result already required by the baseline rather than selecting among legally plausible scopes. The operation is therefore draft-classified as codify, subject to human confirmation because the baseline_set_for resolver is not implemented.

OP-098.defect_title: CIP identity-verification timing differs between bank rule and broker-dealer rule

operation.parameters: Relation type: parallel-sector-variant of the same CIP identity-verification-timing pillar element; annotate the divergence (bank: 'within a reasonable time after'; broker-dealer: 'within a reasonable time before or after') as an intentional sector-specific threshold, not a drafting error to be normalized away.
operation.proposal: At blueprint level, link the bank CIP verification-timing obligation and the broker-dealer CIP verification-timing obligation as parallel variants of one shared CIP pillar element, and record that the timing thresholds differ by sector: the bank rule permits verification only 'within a reasonable time after the account is opened,' while the broker-dealer rule additionally permits verification 'before' account opening. The relation makes the divergence visible and traceable without asserting the two are identical.
operation.rationale: The refactor pass fixes the drawing, not the bricks. The defect frames the added 'before' window as a scope/threshold mismatch, but the two spans are genuinely different regulatory text in two distinct parts (1020 for banks, 1023 for broker-dealers), each independently in force. Neither source states supersession of the other, so under P3.5 harmonizing them by deleting or overriding the 'before' window would be a policy choice, not a meaning-preserving refactor. RELATE-OBLIGATION exposes the parallel structure and the deliberate delta so a reader sees one CIP pillar with a sector-specific timing threshold, which is the honest blueprint representation of what the law actually requires.

citations.quote: within a reasonable time after the account is opened.
within a reasonable time before or after the customer's account is opened.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative baseline consists of current, sector-specific federal CIP regulations issued under the BSA framework. For banks subject to 31 CFR 1020.220, the CIP must provide verification within a reasonable time after account opening. For broker-dealers subject to 31 CFR 1023.220, the CIP must provide verification within a reasonable time before or after account opening. Applicability keeps the provisions in separate actor/activity cells, and neither provision supersedes or imports the other’s timing threshold. Their current status and distinct text therefore require preserving both thresholds; normalizing them would change at least one cell. The proposed relation does not alter either duty and accurately exposes their parallel CIP function and sector-specific delta. It is classified as clarify rather than codify because the regulations do not themselves state that the provisions are “parallel-sector variants” or characterize the divergence as intentional; that relationship is a supported blueprint-level interpretation. “Intentional” should be understood only as an instruction to preserve the legally operative difference, not as a claim about undocumented regulatory purpose. This is not fill_gap because no omitted operative duty is being made explicit, and it is not change so long as the relation neither equates the timing rules nor overrides either threshold.

OP-099.defect_title: Independent-testing frequency threshold mismatch across program instruments

operation.parameters: Relation type: SAME-PILLAR-DIVERGENT-THRESHOLD. Group the four independent-testing/independent-review obligations under one blueprint pillar node ('independent testing/review') and annotate each with its instrument-specific frequency threshold: FINRA-3310 O5 = annual (calendar-year), biennial for firms not executing customer transactions/holding customer accounts/acting as introducing broker; CAB331-5 = no less frequently than every two years; 31-cfr-1022 = no fixed interval, scope/frequency commensurate with risk; ffiec-man-cp-03 = no regulatory frequency requirement, commensurate with risk profile.
operation.proposal: Draw an explicit cross-instrument relation linking the four independent-testing/independent-review obligations as instances of a single program pillar, each carrying its own frequency threshold. The relation makes the divergence visible and navigable at blueprint level without altering any instrument's stated interval. The blueprint node records that the pillar is common (independent testing conducted by qualified independent parties, not the AML compliance officer) while the frequency parameter is instrument-specific.
operation.rationale: The defect is a drawing problem, not a bricks problem: the same pillar appears four times with materially different frequency thresholds, and nothing in the sources makes them the same. The thresholds genuinely differ across sectors and each is authoritative for its own actor class; there is NO explicit supersession among these instruments (they govern different covered entities under different authorities), so P3.5 newest-wins does not apply and harmonizing to a single interval would be a policy choice that changes what the law requires — out of scope for the refactor pass. RELATE-OBLIGATION resolves the register finding by making the divergence explicit and structured rather than latent, preserving each threshold verbatim.

citations.quote: Provide for annual (on a calendar-year basis) independent testing for compliance to be conducted by member personnel or by a qualified outside party, unless the member does not execute transactions for customers or otherwise hold customer accounts or act as an introducing broker with respect to customer accounts (e.g., engages solely in proprietary trading or conducts business only with other broker-dealers), in which case such "independent testing" is required every two years (on a calendar-year basis);
Provide for independent testing for compliance, no less frequently than every two years, to be conducted by capital acquisition broker personnel or by a qualified outside party;
The scope and frequency of the review shall be commensurate with the risk of the financial services provided by the money services business.

There is no regulatory requirement establishing BSA/AML independent testing frequency. Independent testing, including the frequency, should be commensurate with the ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risk profile of the bank and the bank's overall risk management strategy.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The baseline supports the proposed relation, but no single source expressly creates a cross-sector blueprint node or declares these four provisions to be instances of one ontology-level pillar. Hierarchy and delegation must remain source-specific: FINRA Rule 3310 governs FINRA members and requires calendar-year annual testing, with the stated biennial exception; CAB Rule 331 governs capital acquisition brokers and requires testing at least every two years; 31 CFR 1022 governs MSBs and makes review scope and frequency risk-commensurate without a fixed interval; federal banking-agency program rules establish the bank independent-testing requirement, while the FFIEC manual is nonbinding supervisory guidance explaining that no regulation fixes its frequency and recommending risk-commensurate frequency. Applicability is therefore disjoint rather than conflicting, and there is no supersession basis for replacing one threshold with another. Status controls preclude treating the FFIEC manual as independently creating a bank duty; its use here is limited to describing the absence of a regulatory interval and supervisory treatment of frequency. Grouping the obligations clarifies their common program function and exposes their divergent parameters while preserving each actor-specific rule. It is not fill_gap because the operation adds no missing duty, and it is not change because it neither harmonizes intervals nor extends one sector's threshold to another. Human confirmation remains required because the baseline_set_for resolver is unavailable and the common-pillar relation is a derived characterization rather than express cross-instrument text.

OP-100.defect_title: Independent-testing frequency threshold mismatch across program instruments

operation.parameters: Normalize each independent-testing obligation into a shared element frame: {actor-class, who-may-conduct (independent party), frequency-threshold, frequency-basis (fixed interval vs. risk-commensurate), independence-constraint}. Populate frequency-basis as: FINRA-3310 = fixed (annual/biennial by activity); CAB331 = fixed (>= 2 years); 31-cfr-1022 = risk-commensurate (no fixed interval); ffiec-man-cp-03 = risk-commensurate (no regulatory frequency).
operation.proposal: Recast the four obligations into a common element schema so the frequency field is a directly comparable slot across instruments, exposing that two instruments set fixed intervals and two set risk-commensurate frequency. This makes the mismatch a legible, tabulated distinction rather than an accidental inconsistency, without changing any threshold value.
operation.rationale: The register flags divergent thresholds 'across program instruments'; normalizing the element structure lets the target blueprint present the pillar as one row-set with an explicitly varying frequency column. This is a pure representation change (fix the drawing) — it neither merges the obligations nor alters the required intervals. Composed with the RELATE-OBLIGATION grouping, it yields a coherent pillar view while honoring that the differences are substantive and non-supersessive.

citations.quote: Provide for independent testing for compliance, no less frequently than every two years, to be conducted by capital acquisition broker personnel or by a qualified outside party;

There is no regulatory requirement establishing BSA/AML independent testing frequency. Independent testing, including the frequency, should be commensurate with the ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risk profile of the bank and the bank's overall risk management strategy.

operation.composition_note: Works together with the RELATE-OBLIGATION op: RELATE creates the shared pillar node; NORMALIZE-ELEMENTS gives the node a common element frame in which the frequency thresholds sit as comparable, instrument-tagged slots.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation is a representational normalization, not a substantive harmonization. For each applicable cell, the operative baseline already supplies the instrument-specific content placed into the common slots: FINRA Rule 3310 requires calendar-year annual testing for covered FINRA members, with calendar-year biennial testing for the stated limited-activity firms; CAB Rule 331 requires testing no less frequently than every two years; 31 CFR 1022 requires MSB review scope and frequency to be commensurate with risk and establishes no fixed interval. For banks, the operative banking-agency program rules require independent testing, while the FFIEC manual expressly states that no regulation establishes its frequency and gives a nonbinding supervisory recommendation that frequency should be risk-commensurate. Hierarchy, delegation, and applicability therefore remain instrument- and actor-specific. Status controls must be preserved: the FINRA, CAB, and MSB requirements are mandatory within their respective scopes, whereas the FFIEC frequency statement is guidance and must not be rendered as an independent legal duty. The shared frame merely records those existing differences in comparable, instrument-tagged fields; it does not replace fixed thresholds with a common threshold, extend one sector's rule to another, or supersede exceptions. On that understanding, the baseline already requires or supports every represented value, so the operation codifies the baseline. Human confirmation remains necessary because the baseline_set_for resolver is not implemented and because any implementation that drops modality/source status—especially for the FFIEC entry—could instead create an apparent banking duty not established by regulation.

OP-101.defect_title: Board-approval and FinCEN-availability program element applies inconsistently across sectors

operation.parameters: Create a cross-sector governance-of-program relation node ('program approval / availability') that binds each sector's approval-and-availability element to its source and records the differing approving authority (board of directors; equivalent governing body; senior management; none) and the availability duty's addressee (FinCEN or its designee; Department of the Treasury; not specified).
operation.proposal: At blueprint level, introduce an explicit RELATE-OBLIGATION linkage grouping the divergent program-approval/availability elements so the map shows them as the SAME pillar slot filled differently per sector, rather than as unrelated obligations. The relation records: FFR-regulated banks under 31-cfr-1020(a) carry NO textual board-approval/availability element (the (a) branch omits it); non-FFR banks under 1020(b) carry both board-approval and FinCEN-availability; federal banking-agency rules (OCC 12-cfr-21) add a written/board-approved/minuted duty by the agency's own regulation (the '(3) Complies with the regulation of its Federal functional regulator' hook in 1020(a)); broker-dealers require senior-management approval; MSBs require only written + Treasury-availability with no approval element.
operation.rationale: The defect is a drawing defect: four source families fill one conceptual pillar slot with materially different governance requirements, and the blueprint currently presents them as isolated obligations, obscuring both the pattern and the genuine textual gap (1020(a) omits the element the agency rules supply via cross-reference). RELATE-OBLIGATION is meaning-preserving: it changes nothing the law requires and asserts no equivalence, only that these elements occupy the same functional slot. It surfaces that the OCC/FDIC/NCUA/Fed board-approval duty is what supplies the governance requirement for FFR-regulated banks (via 1020(a)(3)'s cross-reference to the FFR's own regulation), which is why 1020(a) itself is silent. This is a policy-neutral observation, not a resolution of the divergence.

citations.quote: The compliance program must be written, approved by the national bank's or savings association's board of directors, and reflected in the minutes of the national bank or savings association.

Is approved by the board of directors or, if the bank does not have a board of directors, an equivalent governing body within the bank. The bank shall make a copy of its anti-money laundering program available to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network or its designee upon request.

The program shall be in writing, and a money services business shall make copies of the anti-money laundering program available for inspection to the Department of the Treasury upon request.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative sources establish different results in the affected cells: OCC-regulated national banks and savings associations must have a written, board-approved, minuted program under 12 CFR part 21; non-FFR banks must obtain board or equivalent-governing-body approval and provide the program to FinCEN or its designee on request under 31 CFR 1020.210(b); FINRA members must obtain written senior-management approval under FINRA Rule 3310; and MSBs must maintain a written program and provide copies to Treasury on request under 31 CFR 1022.210, without an approval element. Section 1020.210(a) does not itself state board-approval or program-availability duties for FFR-regulated banks, instead requiring compliance with the applicable FFR program regulation. Applicability and delegation therefore preserve, rather than eliminate, the sector-specific differences. The proposed relation does not make one sector's requirement applicable to another and must record absences as absences, not implied duties. The baseline directly requires the underlying obligations, but it does not expressly characterize them as one cross-sector 'program approval / availability' pillar slot. That functional alignment is a supported, meaning-preserving interpretation that resolves an architectural ambiguity in the blueprint, so the draft class is clarify rather than codify or fill_gap. It would become change if implemented as a harmonized board-approval or availability requirement. Claims extending the OCC example to FDIC-, Federal Reserve-, or NCUA-regulated institutions, or extending FINRA Rule 3310 to broker-dealers outside its membership applicability, require their own current operative sources and cannot be inferred from the cited targets alone. Human review must also confirm status as of the project's pinned 2026 date.

operation.parameters: Resolve the '(3) Complies with the regulation of its Federal functional regulator governing such programs' cross-reference in 31-cfr-1020(a) to the concrete federal-banking-agency program regulations (here, OCC 12-cfr-21's written/board-approved/minuted duty), making explicit on the blueprint that the governance element for FFR-regulated banks is supplied by the FFR regulation and not by 1020(a) directly.
operation.proposal: Make explicit the pointer by which the apparent gap in 31-cfr-1020(a) (no board-approval/availability element) is filled: 1020(a)(3) requires compliance with 'the regulation of its Federal functional regulator governing such programs', and the OCC rule at 12-cfr-21 supplies the written/board-approved/minuted governance duty. operation.rationale: The defect description reads 1020(a) as omitting board approval 'by the text's own terms' — true of 1020(a) read in isolation, but 1020(a)(3) is a live cross-reference into the FFR program regulations, where the governance duty resides. Resolving this dangling reference is meaning-preserving and corrects a drawing error (a pillar slot that appears empty is actually populated by cross-reference). This does not equalize sectors — MSBs and broker-dealers remain genuinely different — it only completes the FFR-bank branch.

citations.quote: A bank regulated by a Federal functional regulator shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) if it implements and maintains an anti-money laundering program that:

Each national bank and each savings association shall develop and provide for the continued administration of a program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the recordkeeping and reporting requirements set forth in subchapter II of chapter 53 of title 31, United States Code

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: For the intersecting applicability cell—banks regulated by the OCC that are national banks or savings associations—the current federal baseline already supplies the governance element that the blueprint appears to omit. FinCEN’s 31 CFR 1020.210(a)(3) requires an FFR-regulated bank’s AML program to comply with the program regulation of its Federal functional regulator. OCC 12 CFR part 21 is that operative FFR regulation for the covered OCC institutions, and OB-2 expressly requires the compliance program to be written, approved by the institution’s board of directors, and reflected in the minutes. Thus the operation does not create or broaden a governance duty; it makes explicit the legal path by which an existing duty enters the FFR-bank branch. The source establishing the duty is OCC 12 CFR part 21, with 31 CFR 1020.210(a)(3) supplying the cross-reference. Applicability must remain bounded: this resolution establishes the result only for national banks and savings associations within the OCC rule’s scope, not automatically for every FFR-regulated bank, MSB, or broker-dealer. The supplied authorities are operative regulations with verified quotations; no status-control indication suggests reliance on a proposed or superseded rule. Accordingly this is an ADR-005 representational gap fill, subject to human confirmation because baseline_set_for is not implemented.

OP-103.defect_title: NPRM cites '5318(h)(1)' for banks/broker-dealers but '5318(h)' for MSBs — applicability locator mismatch

operation.parameters: Normalize the statutory applicability locator across the bank, broker-dealer, and MSB program sections to a single consistent citation depth. The blueprint should flag both loci as pointing to the same statutory program mandate (31 U.S.C. 5318(h)), record that 5318(h)(1) is the subparagraph within 5318(h) that contains the four-pillar program requirement, and mark the depth divergence as a locator-consistency issue for the Authority to resolve in the citation text.
operation.proposal: At blueprint level, resolve the cross-reference so that the bank/broker-dealer '5318(h)(1)' locators and the MSB '5318(h)' locator are recognized as referring to the same underlying statutory program mandate. The blueprint records a single canonical target (31 U.S.C. 5318(h)) and notes that the program-establishment requirement resides at 5318(h)(1); the MSB citation omitting the subparagraph is a shallower pointer to the same duty, not a different duty. This surfaces the divergence as a citation-depth inconsistency without asserting the two texts impose different obligations.
operation.rationale: This is a refactor-pass locator mismatch (fix the drawing, not the bricks): the same program mandate is cited at different subparagraph depths across sectors. RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE makes the shared target explicit without changing what any provision requires. NOTE ON P3.5: I am NOT choosing which citation depth is 'correct' — the sources do not contain explicit supersession or a statement that the depths are equivalent, so declaring one canonical form is a policy choice reserved to the Authority. The proposal only records that both point to the same statutory locus (5318(h)/(h)(1)) and flags the divergence; picking the harmonized depth is left to the Authority. CIP cross-references within 1023 itself already cite the shallower '5318(h)' form ('anti-money laundering compliance program required under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)'), corroborating that the two depths are used for the same program duty within a single part.

citations.quote: complies with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) and this section if the bank
complies with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) and this section if the money services business

A broker or dealer in securities shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) if the broker-dealer implements and maintains a written anti-money laundering program approved by senior management that:
The CIP must be a part of the broker-dealer's anti-money laundering compliance program required under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h).

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: For each touched sector, the operation concerns only the locator for the federal AML-program-establishment mandate, not the content or applicability of that mandate. In the statutory hierarchy, 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) is nested within 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) and contains the program requirement; therefore a subsection-level reference to 5318(h) and a paragraph-level reference to 5318(h)(1) can identify the same operative statutory locus at different depths. The in-force broker-dealer rule, 31 CFR 1023.210, expressly uses 5318(h)(1), while another operative cross-reference in part 1023 describes the CIP as part of the program required under 5318(h). This supports treating the forms as references to the same broker-dealer program duty. The supplied current-rule and proposed-rule materials show the same depth divergence across banks, MSBs, and broker-dealers, but do not establish an authoritative requirement to use one citation depth uniformly. Applicability remains sector-specific under the governing statute and implementing rules, and the operation neither expands nor contracts it. Status controls matter: the 2026 NPRM may demonstrate a proposed drafting pattern but cannot establish current law. Accordingly, recording the shared statutory locus, preserving that the operative program requirement resides in paragraph (h)(1), and flagging the citation-depth ambiguity is a clarification. Actually selecting and imposing one harmonized citation text would not be baseline-required on this record and would require Authority disposition rather than being treated as codification.

OP-104.defect_title: NPRM cites '5318(h)(1)' for banks/broker-dealers but '5318(h)' for MSBs — applicability locator mismatch

targets.element_ref: interaction: program mandate attachment across sectors

operation.parameters: Add a blueprint relation tagging the bank, broker-dealer, and MSB program-establishment obligations as instances of a common parent duty (the 5318(h) statutory program mandate), so the locator-depth divergence is visible as an attribute of one shared relationship rather than three unrelated citations.
operation.proposal: Relate the sector-specific program-establishment obligations (bank OBL, broker-dealer OBL-1, MSB OBL) as children of a single statutory-mandate node in the blueprint. The relation carries the locator-depth metadata (which sections cite (h)(1) vs (h)), making the mismatch a queryable property of one relationship instead of an accidental artifact of independent extractions.
operation.rationale: The divergence is only a defect because the blueprint currently treats three deem-compliance provisions as separate. Relating them to their common statutory parent makes the inconsistency legible and lets the Authority decide on harmonization. This is meaning-preserving: it asserts only that the provisions attach to the same 5318(h) mandate, which the NPRM's own interaction extraction already states ('tie the AML/CFT program requirement to the statutory program mandate in 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)').

citations.quote: Proposed bank, MSB, and broker-dealer program sections tie the AML/CFT program requirement to the statutory program mandate in 31 U.S.C. 5318(h), though the bank and broker-dealer sections cite '5318(h)(1)' while the MSB section cites '5318(h)' without the subparagraph.

A broker or dealer in securities shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) if the broker-dealer implements and maintains a written anti-money laundering program approved by senior management that:

operation.composition_note: Works together with the RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE op: RELATE-OBLIGATION establishes the shared parent node that RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE annotates with the divergent locators.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The legal hierarchy itself already treats 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) as the parent statutory program mandate, with 31 CFR 1020 (banks), 1022 (MSBs), and 1023 (broker-dealers) as sector-specific implementing/deeming provisions — 31-cfr-1023 OBL-1 explicitly states it deems compliance with '5318(h)(1)'. Read narrowly, asserting that these current-law provisions share a common statutory parent is a fact the baseline already supports (arguably fill_gap under ADR-005, source: 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) plus the deeming clauses in 31 CFR 1020/1022/1023). However, the operation as drafted does not confine itself to that current-law structure: its target list pairs the single current-law obligation (31-cfr-1023 OBL-1) with an interaction extraction from fincen-program-nprm-2026 — a proposed, not-yet-effective rule — and the rationale explicitly leans on 'the NPRM's own interaction extraction' to justify the relation as meaning-preserving. Per spec/20 §3 evidentiary ceilings, a proposed rule can never anchor a claim about what current law already requires; using the NPRM's characterization of the 5318(h)(1)/5318(h) divergence as support for a blueprint relation about the standing statutory hierarchy blurs status controls between current law and pending rulemaking. Compounding this, the primary NPRM citation offered in support is itself marked verified:false, and the operation's prose describes a three-sector (bank/broker-dealer/MSB) relation while the actual targets list only one current-law node (1023 OBL-1) alongside the NPRM node — leaving the intended scope of the relation (current-law-only vs. current-plus-proposed) genuinely indeterminate on the face of the operation. Because the baseline determination turns entirely on which scope is intended, and one of the two readings would violate the evidentiary ceiling while the other would be a legitimate fill_gap/codify move, the cell is indeterminate rather than resolvable — this routes like change and should be flagged to the human classifier for scope clarification before disposition.

OP-105.defect_title: Divergent in-scope actor categorizations across the two enforcement indices

targets.element_ref: in-scope actor categories (Depository Institutions / Money Services Businesses / Securities and Futures)
supervised entities (National banks and their subsidiaries / Federally chartered savings associations and their subsidiaries / Federal branches and agencies of foreign banks / IAPs)

operation.parameters: Assert an is-a / subset relation: the OCC supervised-entity taxonomy (national banks and subsidiaries, federal savings associations and subsidiaries, federal branches/agencies of foreign banks) is a supervisory partition of the same population FinCEN's index labels 'Depository Institutions'; IAPs are a person-level extension, not a coextensive actor category. Record that the two scopes are related-by-jurisdictional-lens over one program population, not conflicting definitions.
operation.proposal: Add an explicit relation edge at blueprint level tying the FinCEN enforcement-index actor category 'Depository Institutions' to the OCC enforcement-index supervised-entity classes. The relation states that the OCC classes are a supervisor-specific decomposition of the depository-institution population FinCEN scopes by financial-institution filter, and that the divergence is an artifact of two different indexing lenses (FinCEN by BSA-covered financial-institution type; OCC by chartering/supervisory jurisdiction plus person-level IAPs) over the same program, not two inconsistent definitions of who is covered.
operation.rationale: D10 is a drawing defect: the same covered population is catalogued under two orthogonal classification schemes (BSA financial-institution type vs. OCC supervisory jurisdiction). Both indices are enforcement evidence, not operative duty sources, so no requirement changes. RELATE-OBLIGATION makes the cross-index relationship explicit without collapsing either taxonomy, preserving that FinCEN's index also enumerates boundary sectors (Casinos, Insurance, etc.) out of this program's scope and that OCC's IAP class has no FinCEN-index counterpart. This fixes the mismatch by drawing the edge rather than editing either scope.

citations.quote: The OCC supervises the following entities and has the statutory authority to take enforcement actions against them:
National banks and their subsidiaries

In the Matter of TD Bank, N.A. and TD Bank USA, N.A. 
 10/10/2024
 
 2024-02 
 Depository Institutions

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation asserts an applicability relationship between FinCEN’s broad enforcement-index label “Depository Institutions” and OCC’s charter/supervisory classes. The supplied sources do not establish that relationship through operative law. Both are enforcement indices, contain no extracted program-establishment obligations, and organize populations for different enforcement purposes. Legal hierarchy and delegation therefore require consultation of the controlling BSA definitions and program rules in 31 U.S.C. and 31 C.F.R. Chapter X, together with OCC charter, supervisory, and enforcement statutes and regulations. Those operative sources must determine whether each class—including subsidiaries and federal branches or agencies of foreign banks—is wholly within, only partly overlaps, or falls outside FinCEN’s relevant depository-institution definition. The proposed subset statement may overreach because an OCC-supervised subsidiary is not necessarily itself a depository institution, while an IAP is a person subject to a distinct enforcement regime rather than an institution bearing the program-establishment duty. Status controls also require the pinned 2026 versions of those operative sources; no proposed rule may cure any omission. The baseline may ultimately support a qualified crosswalk, but the present record cannot determine its exact direction or coverage without exceeding the evidentiary ceiling. Accordingly the draft is unresolved and routes like change pending human comparison of the operative applicability provisions; it is not codify, clarify, or fill_gap on the enforcement-index evidence alone.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: Manual draft posture: the baseline_set_for resolver is not implemented. The operation does not create, expand, or reassign an AML/CFT program duty. It adds a blueprint-level type distinction to prevent an applicability error when aligning two enforcement indices. The OCC index separately describes IAPs as officers, directors, employees, controlling stockholders, agents, and certain other individuals, while listing national banks, federal savings associations, and federal branches or agencies of foreign banks as supervised entities. That supports treating IAPs as person-level enforcement subjects rather than entity-level covered institutions. The FinCEN index, by contrast, organizes matters through institution or sector categories such as Depository Institutions, Money Services Businesses, and Securities and Futures. The sources therefore support the proposed distinction, but the mixed OCC list and cross-index alignment leave the typing implicit; making it explicit is clarification. Legal hierarchy and delegation do not establish a new program-establishment obligation for IAPs, and applicability remains limited to the OCC enforcement-index context rather than converting IAPs into a FinCEN financial-institution category. No status control or proposed rule is relied upon. Because the support consists of enforcement-index material, it cannot independently establish an operative duty; accordingly, this draft does not treat the operation as codifying or filling a duty gap. The explicit assertion of disjointness is an analytical modeling conclusion supported by the person-versus-entity descriptions, not a new legal rule.

OP-107.defect_title: Risk assessment framed as non-mandatory in RA item but embedded as expectation elsewhere

operation.parameters: Establish an explicit relation: the compliance-program 'commensurate with risk profile' obligation (OB-03) and the internal-controls 'incorporate the BSA/AML risk assessment' obligation (cp-02-O3) each PRESUPPOSE the risk-assessment activity described in ffiec-man-ra (OBL-03). The relation is 'the program/controls obligations depend on the risk assessment as an input'.
operation.proposal: Draw an explicit dependency edge in the blueprint linking the risk-assessment obligations in ffiec-man-ra to the program-level 'commensurate with risk profile' obligation (OB-03) and the internal-controls obligation to 'incorporate the bank's BSA/AML risk assessment' (cp-02-O3). This surfaces that the same risk-assessment activity treated as 'not a specific legal requirement' in the RA item is the very input the CP/IC obligations require the program and controls to be built around, so the apparent scope/applicability mismatch is a cross-reference relation rather than a contradiction.
operation.rationale: This is a refactor (drawing) fix, not a change to what the law requires. The RA item's 'not a specific legal requirement' characterization and the CP/IC items' expectation that the program/controls be commensurate with and incorporate the risk assessment coexist in the sources: the risk assessment is not itself a standalone mandated deliverable, but the program obligations that ARE mandatory ('must establish and maintain', 'must provide for... internal controls') are conditioned on the risk profile/assessment. RELATE-OBLIGATION makes that structural dependency visible without altering any modality. Note the modality asymmetry preserved as-is: OB-03 and cp-02-O3 are framed 'should', while OB-01/OB-05 are 'must' — the relation clarifies the input dependency, it does not upgrade the RA item to mandatory.

citations.quote: While not a specific legal requirement, a well-developed BSA/AML risk assessment assists the bank in identifying ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risks and in developing appropriate internal controls (i.e., policies, procedures, and processes).
To achieve the purposes of the BSA, the BSA/AML compliance program should be commensurate with the bank's ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risk profile.
Incorporate the bank's BSA/AML risk assessment and the identification of ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risks, along with any changes in those risks.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: For the touched U.S. depository-institution cells, the FFIEC examination-manual baseline supports—but does not unambiguously require—the proposed dependency relation. The program item says a bank's program should be commensurate with its risk profile, while the internal-controls item instructs examiners to determine whether controls incorporate the bank's BSA/AML risk assessment. The risk-assessment item describes what that assessment should provide. Read together, these sources support representing risk assessment as an input to risk-aligned program design and supervisory evaluation. Status and hierarchy controls prevent treating that relation as a new standalone operative duty: the manual expressly states that a BSA/AML risk assessment is not a specific legal requirement; the relevant formulations are generally 'should'; and cp-02-O3 is examiner-facing rather than a direct bank obligation. Mandatory program-establishment and internal-controls requirements do not, on the supplied record, independently mandate a particular formal risk-assessment deliverable. Moreover, being commensurate with a risk profile conceptually requires understanding risk but does not unambiguously presuppose the specific assessment described in OBL-03. Accordingly, drawing the edge is a clarification of the manual's cross-item structure only if it preserves those modality, actor, and status distinctions and does not state that a formal risk assessment is independently mandatory. Applicability is limited to banks/depository institutions and their federal supervisory examination; this operation supplies no basis for extending the relation to MSBs, broker-dealers, or FINRA. It is not fill_gap because no cited source establishes a missing standalone bank duty to produce the assessment, and it is not codify because the precise dependency is inferential and qualified rather than unequivocally required.

OP-108.defect_title: Risk assessment framed as non-mandatory in RA item but embedded as expectation elsewhere

operation.parameters: Bind the dangling narrative pointer in ffiec-man-cp-01 ('Refer to the BSA/AML Risk Assessment section...') to the concrete ffiec-man-ra item, so the CP item's risk-profile obligation resolves to the RA item's process description.
operation.proposal: Resolve the explicit cross-reference the CP-01 source already contains ('Refer to the BSA/AML Risk Assessment section and Appendix I - Risk Assessment Link to the BSA/AML Compliance Program') to point at ffiec-man-ra as the authoritative description of the risk-assessment process the program must be commensurate with. This makes the applicability question ('is a risk assessment required?') answerable by following a resolved link: the RA process is the definitional source for the risk profile that the mandatory program obligations reference.
operation.rationale: The mismatch is partly a drawing artifact: CP-01 gestures at the RA section by prose reference but the blueprint left it unresolved, so a reader sees 'must be commensurate with risk profile' in one item and 'not a specific legal requirement' in another with no linking structure. Resolving the cross-reference is a pure drawing fix that preserves both source characterizations and lets classification see them as one coordinated structure.

citations.quote: Refer to the BSA/AML Risk Assessment section and Appendix I - Risk Assessment Link to the BSA/AML Compliance Program for more information.
This section is designed to provide standards for examiners to assess the adequacy of the bank's BSA/AML risk assessment process.

operation.composition_note: Works with the RELATE-OBLIGATION op: the resolved cross-reference is the anchor along which the dependency relation is drawn.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation is codifying only if limited to the documentary cross-reference already present in ffiec-man-cp-01. That source expressly directs readers to the BSA/AML Risk Assessment section, and ffiec-man-ra supplies the referenced process description and examiner standards. Binding that existing pointer does not alter actor, activity, or federal depository-institution applicability and is already required by the source structure. Hierarchy and status controls limit the effect: both items are FFIEC examination-manual material, and their linkage cannot elevate guidance or examiner expectations into an independent operative bank duty. In particular, OB-03 and the bank-facing risk-assessment statements use “should,” while the RA section characterizes the assessment as not itself a specific legal requirement. The resolved link therefore may show how the manual coordinates a risk-commensurate compliance program with the risk-assessment process, but it may not establish that a formal risk assessment is independently mandatory or designate ffiec-man-ra as operative law. The mandatory program and internal-control duties remain anchored in applicable statutes and regulations, not in the cross-reference. Applicability is confined here to federally supervised U.S. depository institutions; this operation does not reach MSBs, broker-dealers, or the FINRA layer. If the proposal’s phrases “authoritative description” or “is a risk assessment required?” are implemented as a current-law conclusion rather than as navigation, that added semantic effect would require separate classification and would likely be change or unresolved.

OP-109.defect_title: Applicability mismatch on whether CIP/CDD are program-establishment obligations

operation.parameters: Relation type: program-pillar obligation that is DISCHARGED-VIA the CIP/CDD/beneficial-ownership coordination layer. Annotate OB-09 and OB-10 with a dual-classification marker: (a) they ARE program-establishment content per the source (the program 'must include' them), and (b) their substantive requirements live in the CDD/CIP coordination layer per ratified scope.
operation.proposal: Attach an explicit relation between the program-establishment obligations OB-09 (CIP) and OB-10 (ongoing CDD / beneficial ownership) and the coordination-layer regimes for CIP/CDD/beneficial ownership. The relation records that the FFIEC manual makes 'including CIP/CDD procedures' a mandatory attribute OF the compliance program itself, while the detailed operational content of CIP/CDD/beneficial ownership is scoped to the coordination layer. This resolves the framing mismatch by making the linkage explicit rather than forcing one classification.
operation.rationale: The defect is an applicability mismatch, not a substantive conflict: the source unambiguously states the program 'must include' CIP and 'must also include' CDD/beneficial-ownership procedures, so at blueprint level these ARE program-establishment obligations. The ratified scope's treatment of CDD as a 'coordination layer' concerns where the operational duties are detailed, not whether the program must contain the procedures. RELATE-OBLIGATION lets both framings stand true simultaneously by drawing the edge between the pillar obligation and the coordination-layer regime, fixing the drawing without changing what the law requires. This is a meaning-preserving cartographic move.

operation.proposal: Split the overloaded blueprint term 'the agencies' into two version-indexed definitions keyed to the issuing instrument, so that the four-agency framing (2024 NPRM + companion FRB SR letter) and the three-agency framing (2026 NPRM) are each represented by their own explicit membership set rather than a single ambiguous label. operation.parameters: Establish two distinct, non-overlapping canonical population terms and record their relation: 'covered institutions' = full BSA AML-program filer set (all of 31 CFR 1020.210(a) banks through 1030.210), per the national-priorities instrument; 'covered NBFIs' = the subset excluding banks with a Federal functional regulator (31 CFR 1020.210(b), 1021.210, 1022.210, 1023.210, 1024.210, 1025.210, 1026.210, 1027.210, 1028.210, 1029.210, 1030.210), per the nonbank statement. Note that 'covered NBFIs' is a proper subset of 'covered institutions', not a competing definition of the same term.
operation.proposal: Canonicalize the two population terms so the blueprint records that 'covered institutions' and 'covered NBFIs' name different (nested) sets rather than presenting an apparent conflict over who the Priorities regime reaches. The national-priorities instrument uses the umbrella 'covered institutions' (all AML-program filers including banks); the nonbank statement scopes to 'covered NBFIs', whose footnote 4 CFR list is the same enumeration MINUS 1020.210(a) banks, and which the statement itself says is addressed separately for banks by a parallel FBA statement.
operation.rationale: The D10 'mismatch' is a drawing defect, not a substantive one: the sources do not disagree about scope, they use two coordinated terms for two intentionally different sets. The nonbank statement's footnote 4 CFR list omits 1020.210(a) (banks) while the national-priorities footnote 6 list includes it, and the statement text expressly routes banks to a separate parallel statement. Making the subset relation explicit removes the appearance of conflict without changing any requirement.

The national-priorities instrument defines “covered institutions” as all financial institutions required by the cited BSA regulations to maintain an AML program, expressly including 31 CFR 1020.210(a) and (b) through 1030.210. The nonbank statement defines “covered NBFIs” through an enumeration that omits 1020.210(a), retains 1020.210(b), and routes banks covered by the parallel bank statement separately. Comparing those enumerations necessarily makes covered NBFIs a proper subset of covered institutions; the surface label “non-bank” does not override the cited applicability provisions. Thus recording two different canonical terms and their subset relation reproduces, rather than supplements or changes, the baseline. The operation must not describe the populations themselves as non-overlapping, because a proper subset overlaps its superset; “distinct/non-overlapping” is supportable only as an instruction not to conflate the two labels. Hierarchy and delegation are respected because the official instruments apply the statutory Priorities framework by reference to existing AML-program regulations. Status controls remain material: neither instrument creates a pre-effective-date incorporation duty, and the nonbank statement additionally records examination forbearance until final regulations become effective. Canonicalization must preserve those triggers and cannot convert future-rule language into current operative program duties. This is not ADR-005 fill_gap because no otherwise unstated duty is being made explicit; it is a direct normalization of expressly enumerated applicability sets.

OP-125.defect_title: CAB Rule 331 applicability is elective while FINRA Rule 3310 applies to all members, for parallel program duties

operation.parameters: Relation type: parallel-program-duty governed by mutually-exclusive applicability conditions. CAB Rule 331 governs a member only where the member (a) meets the CAB definition and (b) affirmatively elects the CAB rule set; FINRA Rule 3310 governs all members by default (subject to more-limited-application-by-terms). operation.proposal: Introduce an explicit blueprint relation linking the CAB Rule 331 program-pillar obligations (CAB331-1..) to the FINRA Rule 3310 program-pillar obligations (OB-3310-*) as substantively parallel duties routed to different actor populations by an applicability selector. The relation records that a member is governed by CAB 331 only if it meets the CAB definition AND elects the CAB rule set, whereas 3310 applies to all members unless more limited by its terms. This makes the scope/threshold difference a first-class, navigable feature of the blueprint rather than an implicit divergence between two instruments.
operation.rationale: The defect is a drawing problem, not a bricks problem: two instruments carry the same substantive program pillars but attach to different actor populations under different applicability conditions, and the blueprint does not currently express what selects between them. RELATE-OBLIGATION is meaning-preserving — it neither changes what CAB 331 or 3310 require nor which entities they bind; it only records the parallelism and the selector (CAB definition + election vs. all-members-default). The sources state the selector directly: FINRA adopted a separate rule set for firms that meet the CAB definition 'and that elect to be governed under this rule set,' while the consolidated FINRA Rules 'apply to all member firms, unless such rules have a more limited application by their terms.'

This makes explicit that sector-specificity and exemptions from the pillars duty arise at the rule/exemption layer (implementing regs, SRO rules, and the (h)(2) exemption power) rather than from the statutory duty text itself — directly addressing the extraction note.
