draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The verified, enacted text of 31 U.S.C. § 5318(h)(2) directly supports separating the Secretary’s permissive exemption authority from the standards-setting authority: after consultation with the appropriate Federal functional regulator, the Secretary may exempt a financial institution that is not subject to 31 CFR part 103 or a successor rule, for so long as that condition persists. Factoring that clause into a distinct node therefore preserves the legal hierarchy, delegation, condition, and temporary duration of the authority. The proposed relationship to OBL-1 is less determinate. Section 5318(h)(2) authorizes exemption from “those standards,” while OBL-1 states the general program-establishment duty for each statutorily defined financial institution. The text does not unambiguously say that an eligible institution is automatically removed from OBL-1’s population; the power is permissive, must be exercised, and is conditioned on part-103 status. Actual sector applicability also depends on the statutory definition in § 5312 and operative implementing or exemption rules. Accordingly, the baseline supports depicting § 5318(h)(2) as a scope-tailoring mechanism, but the edge should not imply a self-executing or blanket exemption from OBL-1, erase § 5312’s statutory thresholds, or treat uncited SRO rules as exercises of Treasury’s exemption power. OP-141.defect_title: The complete independent-testing obligation for members must be assembled from Rule 3310(c) plus Supplementary Material .01

operation.parameters: Consolidate Rule 3310(c) (frequency + who conducts), Supplementary Material .01(a) (more-frequent-if-warranted), .01(b) (working-knowledge requirement), and .01(c) (exclusion list) into a single composite independent-testing obligation carrying all three normative elements: (1) frequency/threshold with the proprietary-only exception, (2) tester-qualification (working knowledge of the BSA and implementing regulations), (3) tester-independence prohibition (excluded persons).
operation.proposal: Merge the fragmented independent-testing elements into one composite obligation at blueprint level so the full duty (frequency, qualified-tester knowledge, and personnel-conflict prohibition) is stated in a single provision rather than assembled by cross-reading 3310(c) and Supplementary Material .01. Preserve each element's modality distinction: the frequency and independence elements are mandatory ('must'/'may not'), while the more-frequent-testing element remains hortatory ('should'). No requirement is added, removed, or strengthened; this is a drawing fix that co-locates duties the sources already impose and links via the '.01 ... pursuant to Rule 3310(c)' cross-reference.
operation.rationale: The defect is that the complete testing duty is nowhere stated whole; guidance restatements capture only frequency. The Supplementary Material itself declares it operates 'pursuant to Rule 3310(c),' so merging is meaning-preserving assembly, not a change to what the law requires. Because the three elements carry different modalities (mandatory frequency/exclusion vs. 'should' for extra testing), the merge must retain those modalities distinctly rather than flatten them.

citations.quote: Provide for annual (on a calendar-year basis) independent testing for compliance to be conducted by member personnel or by a qualified outside party, unless the member does not execute transactions for customers or otherwise hold customer accounts or act as an introducing broker with respect to customer accounts (e.g., engages solely in proprietary trading or conducts business only with other broker-dealers), in which case such "independent testing" is required every two years (on a calendar-year basis);

Independent testing, pursuant to Rule 3310(c), must be conducted by a designated person with a working knowledge of applicable requirements under the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations.

Independent testing may not be conducted by:
(1) a person who performs the functions being tested,
(2) the designated anti-money laundering compliance person, or
(3) a person who reports to a person described in either subparagraphs (1) or (2) above.
All members should undertake more frequent testing than required if circumstances warrant.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative FINRA baseline already requires the composite output. Rule 3310(c), applicable to FINRA members, establishes independent testing by member personnel or a qualified outside party and sets the calendar-year frequency: annually for members with the specified customer-facing activities and every two years for the proprietary-only/no-customer-account category. Supplementary Material .01 expressly applies “pursuant to Rule 3310(c)” and supplies the remaining controls: the designated tester must have working knowledge of the BSA and implementing regulations, and testing may not be performed by the functions-tested personnel, the AML compliance person, or a person reporting to either. It also states that members “should” test more frequently when circumstances warrant. As an operative SRO rule and supplementary material within the SEC-overseen federal securities framework, these provisions govern the same member testing activity and can be assembled at blueprint level without relying on lower-status guidance. The operation preserves applicability, the proprietary-only exception, and each source modality: mandatory frequency and qualification, prohibitory independence controls, and hortatory more-frequent testing. It therefore neither creates a duty nor strengthens the advisory element. The baseline already requires exactly the mandatory output and supports the separately labeled recommendation, so this is a meaning-preserving codification rather than fill_gap or change. This remains a draft for human confirmation because baseline_set_for is not implemented.

OP-143.defect_title: Sector-specific program 'pillars' obligation assembled only by reading statute plus implementing regulations/SRO rules not present in the statutory text

operation.parameters: Establish an explicit blueprint relation node linking the generic base pillars duty (5318(h)(1)/OBL-1), the statutory-purpose statement (5311/5311-OB-01), and the reasonably-designed/risk-based gloss (AMLA OB-2), tagging OBL-1 as the operative base obligation and 5311-OB-01 as purpose-only (non-operative).
operation.proposal: Create a typed relation across the three instruments that presently must be read together to state the base pillars duty: mark 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) (OBL-1) as the operative source of the base 'each financial institution shall establish' program duty and its four minimum elements; mark 31 U.S.C. 5311(2) (5311-OB-01) as a statement of purpose only, not an independent operative duty; and mark AMLA-2020 OB-2 as the 'reasonably designed / risk-based' qualifier on OBL-1. The relation records that the base duty is generic ('each financial institution') and does NOT itself carry sector-specificity.
operation.rationale: The defect is that the base pillars obligation is not stated in any single instrument and is assembled across statute plus a purpose clause plus the AMLA gloss. This is a drawing defect, not a bricks defect: no legal requirement changes. RELATE-OBLIGATION makes the assembly explicit at blueprint level so a reader sees which instrument carries the operative duty (5318(h)(1)), which is purpose-only (5311), and which supplies the risk-based qualifier (AMLA), instead of silently inferring it. Note 5311-OB-01's modality is mislabeled 'conditional' in the extraction though the source is a purpose clause; the relation flags it as purpose-only to prevent it being read as an independent duty.

citations.quote: In order to guard against money laundering and the financing of terrorism through financial institutions, each financial institution shall establish anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism programs, including, at a minimum-

(2) prevent the laundering of money and the financing of terrorism through the establishment by financial institutions of reasonably designed risk-based programs to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism;
reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the requirements of this subchapter and regulations promulgated under this subchapter

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The federal baseline supports the proposed relation, but its legal force must be represented carefully. Under hierarchy and status controls, 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) is the operative source: its mandatory “each financial institution shall establish” language creates the generic AML/CFT program duty and four minimum elements. Section 5311(2) is expressly a statutory-purpose provision and does not independently impose that duty; correcting the extraction’s “conditional” treatment is supported by the source’s status. The AMLA risk-based/reasonably-designed language supports a relationship to programs described in 5318(h)(1), but it appears in the statutory factors that Treasury and appropriate federal functional regulators must consider when setting standards and supervising or examining compliance. Its “should” formulation therefore must not be modeled as an independent, directly enforceable institution duty without additional operative authority. The relation is a clarification if it preserves that indirect/qualifying status; treating OB-2 as itself adding a mandatory fifth pillar would be a change. Applicability to depository institutions, MSBs, and broker-dealers depends on statutory definitions and sector implementing regulations, with FINRA rules adding the SRO layer for members. The three targeted items do not themselves establish that complete sector-specific applicability, so the relation correctly must remain generic and must not imply that it replaces sector rules, exceptions, or delegations. No new program-establishment duty or sector coverage is created by the operation.

operation.parameters: Resolve the pointer chain by which sector-specificity is supplied: 5318(h)(2) authorizes the Secretary (after consultation with the Federal functional regulator) to prescribe minimum standards and to exempt institutions not subject to 31 C.F.R. part 103 (successor: part 1010 et seq.); AMLA uses the MSB cross-reference to 31 C.F.R. 1010.100(ff). FINRA SRO layer) is completed only in those external implementing instruments, which are within scope but not present in the statutory excerpts here.

RESOLVE-CROSS-REFERENCE surfaces the delegation and pointer that hand off to the CFR/SRO layer, so the blueprint no longer implies the statute alone states the sector-applied duty. citations.quote: The Secretary of the Treasury, after consultation with the appropriate Federal functional regulator (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act), may prescribe minimum standards for programs established under paragraph (1), and may exempt from the application of those standards any financial institution that is not subject to the provisions of the rules contained in part 103 of title 31, of the Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor rule thereto, for so long as such financial institution is not subject to the provisions of such rules.

operation.composition_note: Works with the RELATE-OBLIGATION op: that op fixes which instrument carries the base duty; this op fixes where the sector-specific completion lives.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation reproduces an existing federal authority and applicability chain rather than altering an operative duty. At the statutory level, 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) imposes the general program-and-pillars duty on each financial institution. Section 5318(h)(2) expressly authorizes the Secretary, after consultation with the appropriate Federal functional regulator, to prescribe minimum standards and ties exemption authority to coverage under former 31 C.F.R. part 103 or a successor rule. The enacted AMLA text expressly identifies money services businesses through 31 C.F.R. 1010.100(ff). At the implementing level, the sector-applied obligations and applicability controls are supplied by current FinCEN rules, including Parts 1020, 1022, and 1023, and, for FINRA members, the applicable SRO rule layer, including FINRA Rule 3310. Thus the legal hierarchy already consists of a generic statutory duty, delegated rulemaking authority, regulatory sector definitions and program rules, and an additional broker-dealer SRO layer. The proposed annotation accurately records that architecture and does not create a new institution, pillar, regulator, or standard. Applicability remains controlled by each implementing rule's definitions, coverage, exemptions, effective status, and the institution's regulatory/SRO status; the annotation must not imply that 5318(h)(2) itself independently imposes every sector-specific requirement. Subject to confirming those instruments are effective on the pinned 2026 date, each touched cell already receives the stated cross-reference chain from operative law. This is therefore a codification of the baseline's distributed structure, not gap-filling legislation or a substantive change.

Thus the baseline supports treating each level as a singleton but does not itself require the blueprint-specific choice to suppress the enacted ordinal labels. Flattening them only in the derived blueprint, while retaining the statutory text and a provenance note describing the non-consecutive enacted structure, resolves a representational ambiguity without purporting to amend the statute. draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation adds more than a neutral drawing relation: “duty-currently-in-default” asserts a present statutory breach. At the controlling level, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(h)(4)(C), added by AML Act § 6101, requires the Secretary, at least once every four years, to “review and, as appropriate, update” the national priorities. That differs from an unconditional duty to publish updated Priorities every four years. The quoted 2021 FinCEN guidance says FinCEN “will update” the Priorities, but guidance cannot remove the statute’s “as appropriate” qualification or by itself establish that failure to issue a replacement constitutes statutory default. The supplied materials also do not establish the relevant delegation from the Secretary to FinCEN or show whether a timely review occurred and concluded that an update was not appropriate. Applicability is principally to the federal official responsible for reviewing and, as appropriate, updating the Priorities; the annotation does not itself alter institution-level program duties. As a status matter, no cited source provides automatic expiration or revocation of the June 30, 2021 instrument, so describing it as not revoked is supported, but “stale” is evaluative and “in default” is not established merely by the absence of a superseding publication. The baseline therefore requires a periodic review and a conditional update, while the proposed relation records an unconditional missed-update breach. The combined operation should route as change unless the human classifier obtains controlling authority establishing an unconditional update duty plus official evidence that no qualifying review or update occurred by the pinned date.

OP-180.defect_title: Broker-dealer TIN recordkeeping duty tied to obsolete date window

operation.parameters: Separate the MSB program compliance-date clause (§ 1022.210(e)) into (a) an operative standing duty to have an AML program in place and (b) an obsolete/spent one-time transitional trigger 'the later of July 24, 2002' fixed anchor.
operation.proposal: At blueprint level, factor § 1022.210(e) into its two components: the durable operative content (a newly-established MSB must have a complying AML program in place by the end of the 90-day period beginning the day after it is established) and the spent absolute-date component ('the later of July 24, 2002'). Mark the July 24, 2002 anchor as a transitional/spent provision that no longer supplies the operative deadline for any MSB established after that date, while preserving the still-live rolling 90-day-from-establishment trigger. This is a drawing fix: the standing 90-day duty is unchanged.
operation.rationale: As of the pinned 2026 date, 'the later of July 24, 2002 and the end of the 90-day period' resolves for every currently-establishable MSB to the 90-day period, because July 24, 2002 is always the earlier of the two. FACTOR-EXCEPTION isolates the spent absolute date without deleting any live obligation content, so the operative requirement (program in place within 90 days of establishment) is preserved exactly. This does not change what the law requires; it separates archaic scaffolding from the live rule.

citations.quote: A money services business must develop and implement an anti-money laundering program that complies with the requirements of this section on or before the later of July 24, 2002, and the end of the 90-day period beginning on the day following the date the business is established.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The controlling federal baseline is the operative FinCEN regulation at 31 C.F.R. § 1022.210. Section 1022.210(a) expressly requires an MSB to develop, implement, and maintain an effective AML program, while § 1022.210(e) expressly requires compliance by the later of July 24, 2002, or the end of the 90-day period beginning the day after establishment. For an MSB established after July 24, 2002—and therefore for any newly established MSB as of the pinned 2026 date—the later date is necessarily the rolling 90-day deadline. Factoring the clause into durable and spent transitional components thus reproduces the result already required by the regulation; it does not create, extend, or relax a duty. Applicability remains limited to money services businesses covered by § 1022.210. Status controls also require retaining the absolute-date language as historical transitional scaffolding rather than treating it as repealed or deleting it from the source representation. The move is codification rather than fill_gap because both the AML-program duty and its rolling compliance deadline are explicit in the regulation, and it is not clarify because the date comparison is determinative rather than legally ambiguous. The classification assumes the target blueprint clearly limits the 'spent' characterization to prospective/current applicability and preserves the clause's historical legal effect.

OP-189.defect_title: No stated substantive standard defining an 'adequate' or 'inadequate' risk assessment

operation.parameters: Link the adequacy-triggered examiner duty (OBL-12: 'whenever the bank has not developed a BSA/AML risk assessment, or the BSA/AML risk assessment is inadequate, examiners must develop a BSA/AML risk assessment') to the scattered adequacy-bearing obligations that operationalize what 'adequate/well-developed' means: OBL-07 (effective processes resulting in a well-developed RA), OBL-10 (RA identifies ML/TF risks), OBL-11 (considered all products/services/customers/geographic locations and analyzed information relative to those categories), and OBL-06 (criticism only where a decision impacts adequacy).
operation.proposal: Draw an explicit relation binding the 'inadequate' trigger term in the examiner mandate to the criteria the manual already uses to judge adequacy elsewhere in the same item: whether the bank has effective processes yielding a well-developed RA (OBL-07); whether the RA identifies the bank's ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risks (OBL-10); and whether the bank considered all products, services, customers, and geographic locations and analyzed the information relative to those categories (OBL-11). This makes visible that the adequacy standard is not undefined but distributed across the 'Assessing' obligations, and that OBL-06's adequacy-linked criticism limit references the same standard.
operation.rationale: This is a drawing defect: adequacy criteria exist but are dispersed and not connected to the trigger that turns on them. RELATE-OBLIGATION surfaces the existing linkage without altering any requirement. It does not manufacture a substantive standard the sources lack; it points to the standard the manual already articulates in OBL-07/10/11. The residual gap (no bright-line adequate/inadequate threshold, no required categories, no update frequency) is a genuine indeterminacy in the source, not something the refactor pass may cure — noted in cannot_express.

citations.quote: When evaluating the BSA/AML risk assessment, examiners should focus on whether the bank has effective processes resulting in a well-developed BSA/AML risk assessment.
Examiners should assess whether the bank has developed a BSA/AML risk assessment that identifies its ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risks.

Examiners should also assess whether the bank has considered all products, services, customers, and geographic locations, and whether the bank analyzed the information relative to those risk categories.

When the bank has established an appropriate BSA/AML risk assessment process, and has followed existing policies, procedures, and processes, examiners should not criticize the bank for individual risk or process decisions unless those decisions impact the adequacy of some aspect of the bank's BSA/AML compliance program or the bank's compliance with BSA regulatory requirements.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The applicable baseline is the FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual for federal examination of U.S. depository institutions. Within that same item, OBL-12 mandates examiner action when a bank lacks a risk assessment or its assessment is inadequate, while OBL-07, OBL-10, and OBL-11 direct examiners evaluating an assessment to consider effective processes producing a well-developed assessment, identification of ML/TF and other illicit-finance risks, and consideration and analysis of all products, services, customers, and geographic locations. OBL-06 separately makes adequacy relevant to the limit on examiner criticism. These provisions support treating those considerations as adequacy-bearing, but the baseline does not expressly state that they constitute a single, exhaustive definition of “adequate” or directly bind them to OBL-12’s trigger. The proposed relation therefore makes an implicit, distributed linkage explicit and is best drafted as clarify, not codify or fill_gap. Status controls matter: the source is an examination manual, OBL-12 uses “must” for examiners, and OBL-07/10/11 and OBL-06 use “should”; the relation must not elevate examination guidance into a new binding substantive duty for banks or convert the listed considerations into exclusive bright-line criteria. The baseline retains indeterminacy concerning thresholds, required categories, and update frequency. The operation is applicable only to the depository-institution examination cell represented by this manual, not to MSBs, broker-dealers, or the FINRA layer.

OP-190.defect_title: No stated substantive standard defining an 'adequate' or 'inadequate' risk assessment

operation.parameters: Introduce a blueprint-level defined term 'well-developed / adequate BSA/AML risk assessment' whose meaning is assembled strictly from the manual's existing 'Assessing' criteria: a RA produced by effective processes that identifies the bank's ML/TF and other illicit financial activity risks and reflects consideration of all products, services, customers, and geographic locations with analysis relative to those categories, no single indicator being determinative, based on all pertinent information.
operation.proposal: Coin a defined term anchoring the 'adequate'/'inadequate' language used in the examiner mandate (OBL-12) to a single blueprint node whose content is drawn verbatim-in-substance from OBL-07, OBL-10, OBL-11, OBL-08, and OBL-09, rather than leaving 'inadequate' as an untethered trigger. The definition asserts nothing beyond what these obligations already state.
operation.rationale: The defect is that 'inadequate' operates as a load-bearing trigger with no defined content at the point of use. DEFINE-TERM is meaning-preserving here because every clause of the assembled definition traces to an existing 'should assess'/'should focus' obligation in the same item; it re-expresses, not augments. Note honestly: the manual expressly disclaims a bright-line standard ('no required risk categories', 'no requirement to update ... on a continuous or specified periodic basis'), so the defined term captures a process/coverage standard, not a pass/fail metric. It cannot make the standard more determinate than the source without changing what the manual requires.

Examiners should not take any single indicator as determinative of the existence of a lower- or higher-risk profile for the bank.

operation.composition_note: Only meaningful if composed with the RELATE-OBLIGATION move above, which supplies the linkages the defined term summarizes.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The touched baseline is the FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual layer for federal examination of U.S. depository institutions. It already uses “inadequate” as the trigger for the examiner mandate to develop a risk assessment (OBL-12) and supplies related evaluative considerations: effective processes producing a well-developed assessment (OBL-07), identification of ML/TF and other illicit-finance risks (OBL-10), consideration and analysis of all products, services, customers, and geographic locations (OBL-11), no single determinative indicator (OBL-08), and consideration of all pertinent information (OBL-09). These provisions support reading adequacy through those process and coverage considerations, but they do not expressly define “adequate” or state that the listed considerations form a closed or dispositive test. The manual also disclaims bright-line risk categories and a prescribed update frequency. Accordingly, the baseline supports the proposed semantic linkage ambiguously rather than already requiring the exact defined-term node, making this clarify rather than codify or fill_gap. Hierarchy and status controls matter: an examination manual guides supervisory evaluation and cannot create or enlarge a bank-level legal duty beyond governing statutes and regulations. The definition must therefore preserve the source modalities, bank-specific judgment, and qualifications and must not convert examiner “should assess/focus” statements into mandatory bank conduct or a pass/fail safe harbor. Applicability is limited to depository-institution risk assessments and their federal examiners; the operation does not establish an equivalent standard for MSBs, broker-dealers, FINRA, or other sectors. No contrary operative requirement is identified.

This tags the transmittal/NPRM-summary nodes as non-source-of-duty and points to the actual authority chain.
operation.rationale: The finding notes SR 24-4 'expressly disclaims creating substantive obligations.' Encoding that disclaimer and the FinCEN-consistency dependency as explicit relations prevents downstream readers from mis-reading a transmittal as the origin of the pillars duty. citations.quote: The interagency statement does not alter existing BSA/AML legal or regulatory requirements, nor does it establish new supervisory expectations.
The Agencies are issuing the proposal for banking organizations to remain consistent with program rule requirements imposed by FinCEN on banking organizations.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operation combines two effects that cannot receive one confident current-law classification on the supplied baseline. First, recording SR 24-4 as a transmittal that creates no substantive duty is supported directly by its verified statement that it neither alters BSA/AML requirements nor establishes supervisory expectations; that relation would codify the source's status control. Second, the proposed 'derives-from / consistent-with' relation is not established as a current-law dependency. The verified text describes why the Agencies are issuing proposed rules and cites FinCEN's proposal under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(4)(D). A proposal cannot establish the operative content or provenance of current duties. Moreover, 'derives-from' and 'consistent-with' are legally distinct: OCC Bulletin 2024-19 identifies independent agency authority, while SR 24-4 states only that the proposed agency rules are intended to remain consistent with FinCEN requirements. The actual statute, final FinCEN rule, final federal-banking-agency rules, and delegations needed to resolve that relationship are absent from the extraction identified by D9. Applicability is limited here to federally regulated banking organizations and does not establish corresponding relations for MSBs or broker-dealers. operation.rationale: The defect is structural: the enforcement/examination node presupposes a binding incorporation node, but the incorporation node is deferred and unfulfilled. RELATE-OBLIGATION makes that presupposition visible on the blueprint without changing what the law requires. The supplied extractions establish only that final regulations were future at the time of the statements; absence of an operative rule from the supplied set does not establish that no final rule became effective by the pinned 2026 date. Because the status control is unresolved, the human classifier cannot determine whether the proposed suspended/currently-inert annotation is still required by the current baseline. draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The current federal statutory baseline supports the relation, but its precise legal characterization is ambiguous. Section 5318(h)(1) expressly requires each applicable financial institution to establish an AML/CFT program containing at least four enumerated elements. Section 5311 states the subchapter’s purpose in terms of financial institutions establishing “reasonably designed risk-based programs,” while section 5318(h)(2)’s standards and supervision factors more directly refer to paragraph (1) programs as reasonably designed and risk-based. Read together under the same statutory hierarchy, these provisions support depicting risk-based design as a qualification of the overall program rather than as a fifth enumerated pillar. Applicability remains controlled by the statutory definition of financial institution, section 5318 exemptions/delegations, and sector-specific implementing rules for depository institutions, money services businesses, and broker-dealers. The proposed edge is nevertheless interpretive: section 5311 is framed as a purpose provision rather than an institution-directed command, and the supplied section 5318 factor text uses “should” within instructions to regulators. Thus the baseline supports, but does not unambiguously require, the exact assertion that 5311-OB-01 is an independent operative obligation that legally scopes OBL-1. The edge should be recorded as a clarifying cross-reference or risk-based qualifier, not as a new pillar or an enlargement of sector-specific duties. If the target treats section 5311 itself as an independently enforceable command, the human classifier should narrow that representation or consider the excess a change.
